514	## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)
515	
516	Logical model below; the physical model follows ADR-0001 (required `manyToOne` `country` relation,
517	`strictRelations: true` already set), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON) and the
518	`strapi-content-modeling` conventions. Names subject to US-03-Q-03.
519	
520	### 7.1 Terms collection type (per country, draft & publish on)
521	
522	| Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
523	|---|---|---|
524	| `title` | string, required, `maxLength: 150` | Spanish, non-blank. Shown as the terms heading and the region's accessible name. |
525	| `body` | `blocks` per ADR-0009 (US-03-Q-02), required | Spanish formatted text. |
526	| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` | ADR-0001; publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |
527	
528	No `key`, `sortOrder`, `isActive` or `version`: unpublishing is how an editor withdraws terms, and
529	the most recently published one wins (US-03-Q-12). No bespoke backend code (no uniqueness
530	middleware).
531	
532	### 7.2 Wire shape and mapping
533	
534	Request (one per summary entry and per "Reintentar", through the proxy, published only, 10 s
535	timeout):
536	
537	```
538	GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=title&fields[1]=body
539	  &fields[2]=publishedAt&sort[0]=publishedAt:desc&pagination[pageSize]=10
540	```
541	
542	Mapping wire → logical `Terms` (boundary parser):
543	
544	| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
545	|---|---|---|
546	| `title` | non-blank string | `title` |
547	| `body` | `blocks` per ADR-0009 (US-03-Q-02): an array whose supported nodes yield at least one non-blank text | `blocks` (the whitelisted, typed node tree) |
548	| `publishedAt` | ISO date-time string | used for ordering only |
549	
550	The parser sorts by `publishedAt` descending itself and does not rely on the server sort. A
551	malformed entry is skipped with a `console.warn` naming the problem, never the text.
552	
553	### 7.3 Seed (summary)
554	
555	Full text in the annex [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md).
556	
557	**Seed rule (human decision, US-03-R1-F01, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21).** The seed creates a
558	country's seed terms (the published document and, for CO, the draft-only document below) **only
559	when that country has no terms document at all**, neither draft nor published. Once an editor has
560	any terms for a country, the seed never creates, updates or republishes terms for that country
561	again: renaming, replacing, unpublishing, or deleting and recreating terms in the Strapi admin
562	survives a restart. The check is per country, so CO and CL are decided independently. Edge case:
563	if an editor deletes every terms document of a country, the next restart seeds the fictitious
564	terms again, because they are the documented starting content. This replaces the earlier
565	"natural key country code + `title`" rule for terms; the seed of other content types is unchanged.
566	
567	| Country | Published | Draft only |
568	|---|---|---|
569	| CO | "Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia" (5 blocks, bulleted list, heading "Condiciones principales") | "Términos y condiciones (borrador)" |
570	| CL | "Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile" (5 blocks, numbered list, heading "Condiciones generales") | — |

634	## 9. Non-functional requirements
635	
636	- **Accessibility (Assessment: "The wizard can be completed using only the keyboard, and fields
637	  have accessible labels"):** focus on the heading on arrival and on confirmation, description
638	  lists for data, a named focusable terms region, a labelled checkbox, a named radio group, a
639	  perceivable disabled "Pagar" with its reason, alerts announced once (AC-16, AC-17). WCAG 2.2 AA;
640	  screen reader pass at HC3.
641	- **Responsive (Assessment: "Works on mobile and desktop"):** 320–1440 CSS px without horizontal
642	  scroll; one column on narrow screens; targets ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (AC-18, manual).
643	- **Multi-country (Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and
644	  Chile"):** no terms text, field label, plan, currency, date format or masking branch per country
645	  in front-end code; dates and prices use the country's `locale` and `currencyCode` from Strapi.
646	- **Security / privacy (Assessment: "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the
647	  browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified"; "Use fictitious data only."):** one
648	  added public permission (§7.4); reads through the GET-only proxy; drafts never anonymous; no
649	  request during payment; no card data; masking at display time; no value, quote number or terms
650	  text in logs; rich text rendered without executing editor input (AC-13, AC-19). Seed and test
651	  data fictitious.
652	- **Persistence (Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not
653	  required."):** ADR-0003 unchanged; US-03 adds nothing to storage and deletes the entry on success.
654	- **Performance:** one terms request per summary entry; summary data comes from content already
655	  loaded by the guards in this page load; the price rule and masking are synchronous pure functions.
656	- **Testing (Assessment: "Unit tests for the relevant logic and at least one e2e test of the full
657	  flow for one country"):** masking, value display, quote number, terms parser and the simulated
658	  payment are unit tested; the CO full-flow e2e is completed end to end (US-03-Q-16).
659	- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, logs and docs English.

# US-03 — Summary and payment · Spec

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story | [story.md](story.md) (verbatim, not edited) |
| Status | Approved |
| Version | 0.1 |
| Author | spec-writer subagent (Claude Opus 5.5) |
| Approved by | v0.1: Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 (HC1 round 1) |
| Related ADRs | [ADR-0001](../../adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (`terms` per country with a required `country` relation; `/:country/resumen`; implementation note: summary route and `summaryStepGuard` registered by US-02), [ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) as amended by [ADR-0005](../../adr/0005-e2e-token-scope-for-relations.md) (public `find` on terms, proxy `/api/terms`, published-only reads, e2e token scope), [ADR-0003](../../adr/0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) (clear on successful payment, keep on rejected payment, terms and payment data never stored), [ADR-0006](../../adr/0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) (typed attributes, `localeTag`), [ADR-0007](../../adr/0007-simulated-price-rule.md) (`calculateFinalPrice` reused), [ADR-0008](../../adr/0008-simulated-payment.md) (simulated payment; resolves US-03-Q-01; Accepted at HC2, 2026-11-21), [ADR-0009](../../adr/0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) (terms rich-text format and safe rendering; resolves US-03-Q-02; Accepted at HC2, 2026-11-21). See §10. |

Sources cited in this spec:

- **Story**: [story.md](story.md).
- **Assessment**: requirements quoted verbatim from the assessment PDF by the orchestrator (not in
  the repository).
- **US-01**: [specs/US-01/spec.md](../US-01/spec.md) v0.5 (Approved): the typed step 1 output and
  reserved keys (§7.3), code-owned copy (§8.1), seed values ([seed-fields.md](../US-01/seed-fields.md)).
- **US-02**: [specs/US-02/spec.md](../US-02/spec.md) v0.1 (Approved): the stored `plan: { key }`,
  the offered plans, price display and formatting (BR-03), what it handed to US-03 (§7.4), and the
  summary route and guard (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15).
- **ADR-0001..0009**: accepted ADRs (precedence level 2; ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 accepted at HC2,
  2026-11-21, for US-03-Q-01 and US-03-Q-02), with the implementation notes in
  [adr/README.md](../../adr/README.md).
- **Reviews** of US-01 (R1..R4) and US-02 (R1, R2): lessons for a new content type (published-only
  router config, anonymous variants in the draft checks, no bespoke backend code where the schema
  suffices) and the `review-checklist` items on rich text, masking and the disabled pay button.

## 1. Summary

Step 3 of the quote wizard. After choosing a plan, a person in Colombia or Chile sees a summary
of their data, their vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price; the document number
is partially masked. From the summary they can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
They read the terms and conditions configured in Strapi for their country, accept them, and pay.
Payment is simulated: no real gateway, no card data. While the simulated payment runs, the pay
button is locked so it cannot be submitted twice. On success the stored quote is cleared and a
confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown; on rejection a clear message is shown and the
person can try again with all their information intact. The same build serves both countries.

## 2. Scope

**In scope**

- The summary page attached to the existing route `/:country/resumen`, behind the existing
  `summaryStepGuard`, without changing the address or the guard (ADR-0001 implementation note).
- Showing step 1 values with their Strapi labels, the chosen plan and its final price (reusing
  `calculateFinalPrice`, ADR-0007, and the US-02 money formatter); masking the document number.
- "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" back to steps 1 and 2.
- A per-country terms content type in Strapi (ADR-0001), its seed for CO and CL
  ([seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md)), public read access (ADR-0002 anticipates `find` and
  `/api/terms`), safe rendering of its formatted text.
- Accepting the terms, the pay button state, the simulated payment (success and rejection), double
  submit prevention, the simulated quote number, the confirmation, and clearing the wizard state on
  success (ADR-0003).
- Loading, error, retry and "not available" states of the terms.
- Keyboard-only use, accessible names, focus management, mobile and desktop layouts.
- Completing the assessment's full-flow e2e `frontend/e2e/us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` with the
  summary, terms, payment and confirmation.

**Out of scope**

- Real payment gateways, card or bank data of any kind, real charges ("Payment is simulated: a
  button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment
  gateways or use real card data.", Assessment).
- Issuing a policy, sending e-mails, PDFs or receipts, storing quotes on a server ("a database is
  not required", Assessment).
- Versioning of the terms or recording which version was accepted (US-03-Q-12).
- Requiring the person to scroll to the end of the terms before accepting (US-03-Q-12).
- Editing data inline on the summary; returning from step 1 straight to the summary (US-03-Q-11).
- Masking any value other than the document number; reformatting typed values (plates, RUT).
- Payment instalments, discounts, taxes.

## 3. Glossary

Terms defined in the US-01 and US-02 glossaries (country context, published, wizard state, typed
step 1 output, reserved key, offered plan, plan key, final price, today, editor) keep their meaning.

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Summary | Step 3 of the wizard at `/:country/resumen`: the person's data, the chosen plan, the terms and the pay action. |
| Terms | The terms and conditions of one country: one published Strapi document of the terms content type (§7.1). |
| Accepting the terms | Checking the code-owned checkbox "Acepto los términos y condiciones". Held in the page's memory only (US-03-Q-10). |
| Masked document number | The display form of the reserved `documentNumber` value defined in BR-02. Computed at display time; never stored (ADR-0003). |
| Simulated payment | A front-end-only stand-in for a payment gateway, with a deterministic outcome and no card data (BR-08, US-03-Q-01). |
| Payment attempt | One activation of "Pagar" that the simulated payment accepts, from the start of processing to its outcome. |
| Quote number | The simulated identifier shown on the confirmation (US-03-Q-07). Not stored and not sent anywhere. |
| Confirmation | What the person sees after a successful payment (US-03-Q-06, US-03-Q-13). |

## 4. Business rules

| ID | Original (source) | Refined (precise, testable) | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| US-03-BR-01 | Story: "The summary shows the policyholder's data, the vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price." | The summary shows, from the typed step 1 output re-derived on entry (US-02-Q-17) and the field configuration of this page load: one row per configured field that has a non-empty value, except `checkbox` fields, with the field's Strapi `label` and its display value (US-03-Q-05). Rows are grouped under "Tu vehículo" (reserved keys `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`) and "Tus datos" (every other key), each in `sortOrder`; a group with no rows is not shown. Display values: `select` → the option's Strapi label; `date` → long Spanish date from the country's `locale` ("15 de mayo de 1990"); `number` → digits with no grouping ("2022"); `text` → as entered (trimmed), except `documentNumber` (BR-02). The chosen plan (`plan.key`) is shown with its name, short description and final price `calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step 1 output, today)` (ADR-0007), formatted as in US-02-BR-03 with the caption "Precio anual" (US-03-Q-14). | US-03-AC-01, US-03-AC-06 |
| US-03-BR-02 | Story: "The document number is shown partially masked." | The value of the reserved key `documentNumber` is shown masked (US-03-Q-04): let *n* be the number of letters and digits in the value; the last *k* = min(4, ⌊n/2⌋) letters and digits stay visible, every earlier letter or digit becomes "•" (U+2022), and every other character (dots, dashes, spaces) stays in place. The same function applies to every country (no country branch). The full number never appears in the DOM, the document title, the URL or a log on the summary or confirmation. The rule applies only to `documentNumber`. | US-03-AC-05 |
| US-03-BR-03 | Story: "From the summary the person can go back to edit their data or change the plan." | "Editar mis datos" navigates to `/<country>/datos` and "Cambiar plan" to `/<country>/planes`, each as a new history entry. Step 1 values and the chosen plan are kept (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-07). The person returns to the summary through the normal flow (step 1 "Continuar" → step 2 → "Continuar"); the price is recomputed. Leaving the summary discards the terms acceptance and the payment simulation choice (US-03-Q-10, Q-11). Both actions are unavailable during a payment attempt (BR-05). | US-03-AC-07 |
| US-03-BR-04 | Story: "The pay button is enabled only after accepting the terms and conditions." | "Pagar" is enabled if and only if the terms of the country are shown (loaded and well-formed) **and** "Acepto los términos y condiciones" is checked **and** no payment attempt is in progress. Otherwise it is perceivably disabled (`aria-disabled="true"`, stays focusable), activating it does nothing, and the reason is shown next to it and linked to it (US-03-Q-17). Unchecking disables it again. | US-03-AC-02, US-03-AC-08, US-03-AC-12 |
| US-03-BR-05 | Story: "The payment cannot be submitted twice." | One activation of an enabled "Pagar" starts exactly one payment attempt. From that moment until the outcome, "Pagar" is disabled and reads "Procesando pago…", the terms checkbox, the simulation choice, "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" are unavailable, and further activations (click, Enter, Space, repeated quickly) start no other attempt. After a success no further attempt is possible; after a rejection a new attempt is possible (BR-08). | US-03-AC-03, US-03-AC-09 |
| US-03-BR-06 | Story: "On successful payment, a confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown." | On a successful attempt the wizard state is deleted (the `quote-wizard` entry and the store's in-memory state; ADR-0003: "Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown") and then the confirmation is shown with a quote number of the format `COT-<country code>-<YYYYMMDD of today>-<6 digits>` (US-03-Q-07), kept in memory only. After that, a reload or the browser back action leads to an empty step 1 of the same country through the existing guards. | US-03-AC-03, US-03-AC-10, US-03-AC-11 |
| US-03-BR-07 | Story context: "accept the terms and conditions, whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi." | The summary shows the terms of the current country: the published terms documents related to that country, the most recently published one if there are several, skipping malformed ones (US-03-Q-12). Draft-only terms and terms of other countries are never shown, and no anonymous caller can read drafts (ADR-0002). Publishing a change is reflected on the next full page load with no code change. The text keeps its formatting (headings, paragraphs, lists, bold, italic) and is rendered without executing anything an editor typed (US-03-Q-02). No terms text exists in front-end code. | US-03-AC-02, US-03-AC-12, US-03-AC-13, US-03-AC-14, US-03-AC-19 |
| US-03-BR-08 | Story context: "Payment is simulated for this test." Story scenario "Rejected payment". Assessment: "Payment is simulated: a button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment gateways or use real card data." | The payment runs entirely in the browser, sends no request and asks for no card, bank or personal data. Its outcome is deterministic and selectable (proposed: a visible "Simulación de pago" choice, US-03-Q-01, ADR needed); processing takes a fixed simulated time (proposed 1.5 s). A rejected attempt shows a clear message, clears nothing (ADR-0003: "Rejected payment: Nothing cleared"), keeps the terms accepted and the simulation choice, and lets the person retry. | US-03-AC-04, US-03-AC-15, US-03-AC-19 |

## 5. Acceptance criteria

Conventions for every scenario:

- "I completed step 1 in Colombia" means the values of US-01-AC-04; "in Chile" means the values in
  the US-02 spec §5 conventions (RUT "12.345.678-5", Nombre completo "Ana Prueba Ficticia", Fecha
  de nacimiento 1990-05-15, Ciudad "Santiago", Patente "BCDF12", Marca "Kia", Modelo "Rio 5",
  Año 2022, consent checked). All values are fictitious seed values.
- "I chose a plan" means "Plan Total" in Colombia and "Plan Protegido" in Chile, then "Continuar"
  on step 2. Today is pinned to **2026-11-21** (final prices $2.310.000 and $528.000, US-02-AC-07).
- Terms are the seed of [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md).
- "The simulated payment fails / succeeds" means the outcome of the simulated payment is set to
  rejected / approved. With the proposed default of US-03-Q-01 that is the "Simulación de pago"
  choice "Pago rechazado" / "Pago aprobado"; if the ADR decides another mechanism, only this
  convention changes.
- Prices are compared with whitespace removed (US-02-BR-03). Code-owned copy is in §8.1.

### US-03-AC-01 — Complete summary

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Complete summary
  Given I completed step 1 in <country> and I chose a plan
  When I reach the summary
  Then the address is "/<code>/resumen" and I see the heading "Resumen de tu cotización"
  And under "Tus datos" I see, in this order: <holder rows>
  And under "Tu vehículo" I see, in this order: <vehicle rows>
  And under "Plan elegido" I see "<plan>", its short description and "<price>" with "Precio anual"

  Examples:
    | country  | code | holder rows | vehicle rows | plan | price |
    | Colombia | co | "Tipo de documento" "Cédula de ciudadanía"; "Número de documento" "••••••5678"; "Nombre completo" "Ana Prueba Ficticia"; "Fecha de nacimiento" "15 de mayo de 1990"; "Ciudad" "Medellín" | "Placa" "ABC123"; "Marca" "Mazda"; "Línea" "3 Touring"; "Modelo (año)" "2022" | Plan Total | $2.310.000 |
    | Chile    | cl | "RUT" "••.•••.678-5"; "Nombre completo" "Ana Prueba Ficticia"; "Fecha de nacimiento" "15 de mayo de 1990"; "Ciudad" "Santiago" | "Patente" "BCDF12"; "Marca" "Kia"; "Modelo" "Rio 5"; "Año" "2022" | Plan Protegido | $528.000 |
```

The consent checkbox is not listed (BR-01). The price equals the one shown on step 2 for the same
data and day (ADR-0007).

### US-03-AC-02 — Terms by country

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Terms by country
  Given I am on the summary in <country>
  When I view the terms and conditions
  Then I see the title "<title>" and the heading "<heading>" of the <country> terms in Strapi
  And I do not see "<other heading>"
  And the pay button is disabled until I accept them

  Examples:
    | country  | title                                                    | heading                 | other heading           |
    | Colombia | Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia     | Condiciones principales | Condiciones generales   |
    | Chile    | Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile     | Condiciones generales   | Condiciones principales |
```

### US-03-AC-03 — Successful payment

```gherkin
Scenario: Successful payment
  Given I am on the summary in Colombia and I accepted the terms
  And the simulated payment succeeds
  When I click pay
  Then the button is locked while the payment is processed: it is disabled and reads "Procesando pago…"
  And I see the confirmation heading "Pago confirmado"
  And I see "Tu número de cotización es" followed by a number matching ^COT-CO-20261121-\d{6}$
```

### US-03-AC-04 — Rejected payment

```gherkin
Scenario: Rejected payment
  Given I am on the summary in Chile and I accepted the terms
  And the simulated payment fails
  When I click pay
  Then I see the message "El pago fue rechazado y no se realizó ningún cobro. Puedes intentarlo de nuevo."
  And I am still on "/cl/resumen" with my data, "Plan Protegido" at "$528.000", and the terms still accepted
  And "Pagar" is enabled again
  When the simulated payment succeeds and I click pay
  Then I see the confirmation heading "Pago confirmado"
```

A reload after the rejection also keeps the data and the plan (ADR-0003); the terms acceptance is
reset by the reload (US-03-Q-10).

### US-03-AC-05 — Masked document number (derived from US-03-BR-02 / Q-04)

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Masked document number
  When the document number <value> is masked
  Then the shown text is <masked>
  And the accessible text is "Número oculto, termina en <tail>"

  Examples:
    | value          | masked         | tail   | why |
    | "1012345678"   | "••••••5678"   | 5678   | 10 digits, last 4 visible |
    | "12.345.678-5" | "••.•••.678-5" | 678-5  | separators stay in place |
    | "123456785"    | "•••••6785"    | 6785   | RUT typed without dots and dash |
    | "12345678-K"   | "•••••678-K"   | 678-K  | check digit K |
    | "12345678"     | "••••5678"     | 5678   | 8 characters |
    | "123456"       | "•••456"       | 456    | 6 characters: half visible |
    | "AB"           | "•B"           | B      | 2 characters |
    | "1"            | "•"            | (none) | nothing visible; accessible text is "Número oculto" |

Scenario: The full number never reaches the page
  Given I completed step 1 in Colombia with Número de documento "1012345678"
  When I reach the summary
  Then the page's DOM, the document title and the address do not contain "1012345678" nor "101234"
```

### US-03-AC-06 — How step 1 values are shown (derived from US-03-BR-01 / Q-05)

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: How step 1 values are shown
  Given the Colombia field configuration of this page load
  And the typed step 1 output has <key> = <value>
  When the summary is shown
  Then <result>

  Examples:
    | key           | value                          | result |
    | documentType  | "CC"                           | the row "Tipo de documento" shows "Cédula de ciudadanía" (the option label) |
    | birthDate     | "1990-05-15"                   | the row "Fecha de nacimiento" shows "15 de mayo de 1990" |
    | vehicleYear   | 2022                           | the row "Modelo (año)" shows "2022" (no thousands separator) |
    | model         | "3 Touring"                    | the row "Línea" is under "Tu vehículo" |
    | dataConsent   | true                           | no row for the consent checkbox |
    | mobilePhone   | null (an editor-added optional text field, left empty) | no row for "Teléfono celular" |
    | mobilePhone   | "3001234567" (editor-added)    | the row "Teléfono celular" is under "Tus datos", in sortOrder, unmasked |
```

### US-03-AC-07 — Edit data or change the plan (derived from US-03-BR-03 / Q-11)

```gherkin
Scenario: Edit my data
  Given I am on the summary in Colombia and I accepted the terms
  When I activate "Editar mis datos"
  Then the address is "/co/datos" and every field shows the value I entered
  When I change "Modelo (año)" to 2015 and activate "Continuar"
  Then I am on "/co/planes" and "Plan Total" is still chosen
  When I activate "Continuar"
  Then the summary shows "Modelo (año)" "2015" and "Plan Total" at "$1.890.000"
  And "Acepto los términos y condiciones" is unchecked and "Pagar" is disabled

Scenario: Change the plan
  Given I am on the summary in Colombia
  When I activate "Cambiar plan"
  Then the address is "/co/planes" and "Plan Total" is chosen
  When I choose "Plan Básico" and activate "Continuar"
  Then the summary shows "Plan Básico" at "$935.000"
```

$1.890.000 = 2 100 000 × 1.00 × 0.90 (vehicle 11 years old, ADR-0007).

### US-03-AC-08 — Pay enabled only with accepted terms (derived from US-03-BR-04 / Q-17)

```gherkin
Scenario: Pay button follows the terms checkbox
  Given I am on the summary in Chile and the terms are shown
  Then "Pagar" is disabled and the text "Acepta los términos y condiciones para pagar." is its accessible description
  When I activate "Pagar"
  Then no payment attempt starts and I stay on the summary
  When I check "Acepto los términos y condiciones"
  Then "Pagar" is enabled and the hint is not shown
  When I uncheck it
  Then "Pagar" is disabled again
```

### US-03-AC-09 — The payment cannot be submitted twice (derived from US-03-BR-05 / Q-08)

```gherkin
Scenario: The payment cannot be submitted twice
  Given I am on the summary in Colombia, I accepted the terms and the simulated payment succeeds
  When I activate "Pagar" three times within 200 ms (click, Enter and click)
  Then exactly one payment attempt is processed
  And during processing "Pagar", the terms checkbox, the simulation choice, "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" cannot be activated
  And exactly one confirmation with one quote number is shown
```

### US-03-AC-10 — Simulated quote number (derived from US-03-BR-06 / Q-07)

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Simulated quote number
  Given today is <today>, the country is <code> and the random source yields <digits>
  When a payment succeeds
  Then the quote number is "<number>"

  Examples:
    | today      | code | digits | number                 |
    | 2026-11-21 | CO   | 482913 | COT-CO-20261121-482913 |
    | 2026-11-21 | CL   | 000007 | COT-CL-20261121-000007 |
    | 2027-01-05 | CO   | 999999 | COT-CO-20270105-999999 |
```

The quote number is not written to `sessionStorage`, not sent in any request and not put in the
address or the document title.

### US-03-AC-11 — The quote is closed after a successful payment (derived from US-03-BR-06 / Q-13, ADR-0003)

```gherkin
Scenario: The quote is closed after a successful payment
  Given I completed a successful payment in Colombia and I see the confirmation
  Then sessionStorage has no "quote-wizard" entry
  When I activate "Nueva cotización"
  Then the address is "/co/datos" and every step 1 field is empty

Scenario Outline: Leaving the confirmation
  Given I completed a successful payment in Colombia and I see the confirmation
  When I <action>
```

## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

Logical model below; the physical model follows ADR-0001 (required `manyToOne` `country` relation,
`strictRelations: true` already set), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON) and the
`strapi-content-modeling` conventions. Names subject to US-03-Q-03.

### 7.1 Terms collection type (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string, required, `maxLength: 150` | Spanish, non-blank. Shown as the terms heading and the region's accessible name. |
| `body` | `blocks` per ADR-0009 (US-03-Q-02), required | Spanish formatted text. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` | ADR-0001; publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

No `key`, `sortOrder`, `isActive` or `version`: unpublishing is how an editor withdraws terms, and
the most recently published one wins (US-03-Q-12). No bespoke backend code (no uniqueness
middleware).

### 7.2 Wire shape and mapping

Request (one per summary entry and per "Reintentar", through the proxy, published only, 10 s
timeout):

```
GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=title&fields[1]=body
  &fields[2]=publishedAt&sort[0]=publishedAt:desc&pagination[pageSize]=10
```

Mapping wire → logical `Terms` (boundary parser):

| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | non-blank string | `title` |
| `body` | `blocks` per ADR-0009 (US-03-Q-02): an array whose supported nodes yield at least one non-blank text | `blocks` (the whitelisted, typed node tree) |
| `publishedAt` | ISO date-time string | used for ordering only |

The parser sorts by `publishedAt` descending itself and does not rely on the server sort. A
malformed entry is skipped with a `console.warn` naming the problem, never the text.

### 7.3 Seed (summary)

Full text in the annex [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md).

**Seed rule (human decision, US-03-R1-F01, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21).** The seed creates a
country's seed terms (the published document and, for CO, the draft-only document below) **only
when that country has no terms document at all**, neither draft nor published. Once an editor has
any terms for a country, the seed never creates, updates or republishes terms for that country
again: renaming, replacing, unpublishing, or deleting and recreating terms in the Strapi admin
survives a restart. The check is per country, so CO and CL are decided independently. Edge case:
if an editor deletes every terms document of a country, the next restart seeds the fictitious
terms again, because they are the documented starting content. This replaces the earlier
"natural key country code + `title`" rule for terms; the seed of other content types is unchanged.

| Country | Published | Draft only |
|---|---|---|
| CO | "Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia" (5 blocks, bulleted list, heading "Condiciones principales") | "Términos y condiciones (borrador)" |
| CL | "Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile" (5 blocks, numbered list, heading "Condiciones generales") | — |

### 7.4 Access (ADR-0002, ADR-0005)

- Public role: add exactly the terms `find` (`api::term.term.find` with the US-03-Q-03 default),
  reconciled in bootstrap; no `findOne`. Justification: the summary must show the country's terms
  (BR-07); data exposed: published terms text, public by nature.
- Router: `createCoreRouter(<terms uid>, publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object
  (US-01-R2-F03).
- Proxy: add `/api/terms` to the GET-only allow-list.
- E2E write token for AC-14 (ADR-0005 general rule): exactly terms `create`, terms `delete` and
  `api::country.country.find`; created and deleted in the Playwright Node process only.

### 7.5 What US-03 reads from the wizard state and the page load

- From the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003): the raw step 1 values (re-derived into the typed
  output with this page load's field configuration, US-02-Q-17) and `plan.key`. US-03 adds
  **nothing** to the entry: no terms acceptance, simulation choice, payment data or quote number.
- From this page load's content: field configuration (labels, option labels, types, `sortOrder`),
  the offered plans (name, short description, `basePrice`), the country (`code`, `currencyCode`,
  `locale`) and the terms.
- On success, the whole entry is deleted and the store's in-memory step 1 values and plan are
  reset (BR-06).

| "Pago confirmado \| Cotizador de seguro de auto" | Confirmation document title |
| "Tu número de cotización es" | Before the quote number |
| "Este es un pago simulado; no se realizó ningún cobro real." | Confirmation notice |
| "Nueva cotización" | Confirmation action |

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment: "The wizard can be completed using only the keyboard, and fields
  have accessible labels"):** focus on the heading on arrival and on confirmation, description
  lists for data, a named focusable terms region, a labelled checkbox, a named radio group, a
  perceivable disabled "Pagar" with its reason, alerts announced once (AC-16, AC-17). WCAG 2.2 AA;
  screen reader pass at HC3.
- **Responsive (Assessment: "Works on mobile and desktop"):** 320–1440 CSS px without horizontal
  scroll; one column on narrow screens; targets ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (AC-18, manual).
- **Multi-country (Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and
  Chile"):** no terms text, field label, plan, currency, date format or masking branch per country
  in front-end code; dates and prices use the country's `locale` and `currencyCode` from Strapi.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment: "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the
  browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified"; "Use fictitious data only."):** one
  added public permission (§7.4); reads through the GET-only proxy; drafts never anonymous; no
  request during payment; no card data; masking at display time; no value, quote number or terms
  text in logs; rich text rendered without executing editor input (AC-13, AC-19). Seed and test
  data fictitious.
- **Persistence (Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not
  required."):** ADR-0003 unchanged; US-03 adds nothing to storage and deletes the entry on success.
- **Performance:** one terms request per summary entry; summary data comes from content already
  loaded by the guards in this page load; the price rule and masking are synchronous pure functions.
- **Testing (Assessment: "Unit tests for the relevant logic and at least one e2e test of the full
  flow for one country"):** masking, value display, quote number, terms parser and the simulated
  payment are unit tested; the CO full-flow e2e is completed end to end (US-03-Q-16).
- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, logs and docs English.

## 10. ADRs

- **Referenced (accepted, binding):**
  1. ADR-0001 — terms content type with a required `manyToOne` `country`; `strictRelations`;
     `/:country/resumen` with `summaryStepGuard` (implementation note: built by US-02, US-03
     attaches the page only); focus on the arriving step's heading. Used by: BR-07, §7.1, AC-16.
  2. ADR-0002 (amended by ADR-0005) — terms `find` on the public role and `/api/terms` on the
     proxy (both anticipated for US-03), `publishedOnlyConfig()`, `no-store`; e2e token with `find`
     on relation targets. Used by: BR-07, §7.4, AC-14, AC-19.
  3. ADR-0003 — entry deleted before the confirmation on success; nothing cleared on rejection;
     terms and payment data never stored; masking at display time. Used by: BR-02, BR-06, BR-08,
     AC-04, AC-11.
  4. ADR-0006 — typed attributes, no free JSON (relevant to the terms `body` format). Used by: §7.1.
  5. ADR-0007 — `calculateFinalPrice` in `frontend/src/app/shared/price-rules.ts`, imported, not
     copied, with the same `CLOCK`. Used by: BR-01, AC-01, AC-07.
  6. ADR-0004 applies to the step 1 form only; the summary's checkbox and radio group are plain
     controls, not a Strapi-driven form.
  7. [ADR-0008](../../adr/0008-simulated-payment.md) — simulated payment (US-03-Q-01; Accepted at
     HC2, 2026-11-21): visible simulation choice, processing time and its injection for tests, the
     gateway service boundary a real gateway would replace, no request and no card data; unit
     test `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts`. Used by: BR-05, BR-06, BR-08, AC-03, AC-04, AC-09, AC-15.
  8. [ADR-0009](../../adr/0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) — terms rich text (US-03-Q-02;
     Accepted at HC2, 2026-11-21): `body` is a Strapi `blocks` attribute rendered by a whitelist
     component through template bindings. Used by: BR-07, §7.1, §7.2, AC-13.
- **Needed (for the architect):** none. The two ADRs this spec asked for (US-03-Q-01, US-03-Q-02)
  are ADR-0008 and ADR-0009 above.
- **Implementation notes (no new decision), if the defaults are accepted:** the terms permission
  name `api::term.term.find` on ADR-0002 (US-03-Q-03). Only if US-03-Q-06 takes the alternative:
  a confirmation route on ADR-0001.

29	## 1. Summary
30	
31	Step 3 of the quote wizard. After choosing a plan, a person in Colombia or Chile sees a summary
32	of their data, their vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price; the document number
33	is partially masked. From the summary they can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
34	They read the terms and conditions configured in Strapi for their country, accept them, and pay.
35	Payment is simulated: no real gateway, no card data. While the simulated payment runs, the pay
36	button is locked so it cannot be submitted twice. On success the stored quote is cleared and a
37	confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown; on rejection a clear message is shown and the
38	person can try again with all their information intact. The same build serves both countries.
39	
40	## 2. Scope
41	
42	**In scope**
43	
44	- The summary page attached to the existing route `/:country/resumen`, behind the existing
45	  `summaryStepGuard`, without changing the address or the guard (ADR-0001 implementation note).
46	- Showing step 1 values with their Strapi labels, the chosen plan and its final price (reusing
47	  `calculateFinalPrice`, ADR-0007, and the US-02 money formatter); masking the document number.
48	- "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" back to steps 1 and 2.
49	- A per-country terms content type in Strapi (ADR-0001), its seed for CO and CL
50	  ([seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md)), public read access (ADR-0002 anticipates `find` and
51	  `/api/terms`), safe rendering of its formatted text.
52	- Accepting the terms, the pay button state, the simulated payment (success and rejection), double
53	  submit prevention, the simulated quote number, the confirmation, and clearing the wizard state on
54	  success (ADR-0003).
55	- Loading, error, retry and "not available" states of the terms.
56	- Keyboard-only use, accessible names, focus management, mobile and desktop layouts.
57	- Completing the assessment's full-flow e2e `frontend/e2e/us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` with the
58	  summary, terms, payment and confirmation.
59	
60	**Out of scope**
61	
62	- Real payment gateways, card or bank data of any kind, real charges ("Payment is simulated: a
63	  button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment
64	  gateways or use real card data.", Assessment).
65	- Issuing a policy, sending e-mails, PDFs or receipts, storing quotes on a server ("a database is
66	  not required", Assessment).
67	- Versioning of the terms or recording which version was accepted (US-03-Q-12).
68	- Requiring the person to scroll to the end of the terms before accepting (US-03-Q-12).
69	- Editing data inline on the summary; returning from step 1 straight to the summary (US-03-Q-11).
70	- Masking any value other than the document number; reformatting typed values (plates, RUT).
71	- Payment instalments, discounts, taxes.

How long does processing take? Is any payment data asked for? | AC-03, AC-04, AC-09, AC-15 and both e2e files depend on it. No card data may be used (Assessment), and the same build serves tests and users, so a test-only switch in code is not available. It is a design that a real gateway would later replace. | Decided by an ADR (§10). Proposal: a visible, code-owned "Simulación de pago (no se realiza ningún cobro)" radio group on the summary with "Pago aprobado" (selected by default) and "Pago rechazado"; no card fields at all. Alternatives for the ADR: a mock gateway page with "Aprobar" / "Rechazar" after "Pagar" (the outcome is not set before the click, so the story's "Given … fails, When I click pay" reads differently); a fake card form with fictitious test card numbers (invites real card entry); a hidden trigger (a magic data value or a URL parameter: not discoverable, test-only behaviour in production). | OK. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 (HC1) |

514	## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)
515	
516	Logical model below; the physical model follows ADR-0001 (required `manyToOne` `country` relation,
517	`strictRelations: true` already set), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON) and the
518	`strapi-content-modeling` conventions. Names subject to US-03-Q-03.
519	
520	### 7.1 Terms collection type (per country, draft & publish on)
521	
522	| Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
523	|---|---|---|
524	| `title` | string, required, `maxLength: 150` | Spanish, non-blank. Shown as the terms heading and the region's accessible name. |
525	| `body` | `blocks` per ADR-0009 (US-03-Q-02), required | Spanish formatted text. |
526	| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` | ADR-0001; publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |
527	
528	No `key`, `sortOrder`, `isActive` or `version`: unpublishing is how an editor withdraws terms, and
529	the most recently published one wins (US-03-Q-12). No bespoke backend code (no uniqueness
530	middleware).
531	
532	### 7.2 Wire shape and mapping
533	
534	Request (one per summary entry and per "Reintentar", through the proxy, published only, 10 s
535	timeout):
536	
537	```
538	GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=title&fields[1]=body
539	  &fields[2]=publishedAt&sort[0]=publishedAt:desc&pagination[pageSize]=10
540	```
541	
542	Mapping wire → logical `Terms` (boundary parser):
543	
544	| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
545	|---|---|---|
546	| `title` | non-blank string | `title` |
547	| `body` | `blocks` per ADR-0009 (US-03-Q-02): an array whose supported nodes yield at least one non-blank text | `blocks` (the whitelisted, typed node tree) |
548	| `publishedAt` | ISO date-time string | used for ordering only |
549	
550	The parser sorts by `publishedAt` descending itself and does not rely on the server sort. A
551	malformed entry is skipped with a `console.warn` naming the problem, never the text.
552	
553	### 7.3 Seed (summary)
554	
555	Full text in the annex [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md).
556	
557	**Seed rule (human decision, US-03-R1-F01, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21).** The seed creates a
558	country's seed terms (the published document and, for CO, the draft-only document below) **only
559	when that country has no terms document at all**, neither draft nor published. Once an editor has
560	any terms for a country, the seed never creates, updates or republishes terms for that country
561	again: renaming, replacing, unpublishing, or deleting and recreating terms in the Strapi admin
562	survives a restart. The check is per country, so CO and CL are decided independently. Edge case:
563	if an editor deletes every terms document of a country, the next restart seeds the fictitious
564	terms again, because they are the documented starting content. This replaces the earlier
565	"natural key country code + `title`" rule for terms; the seed of other content types is unchanged.
566	
567	| Country | Published | Draft only |
568	|---|---|---|
569	| CO | "Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia" (5 blocks, bulleted list, heading "Condiciones principales") | "Términos y condiciones (borrador)" |
570	| CL | "Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile" (5 blocks, numbered list, heading "Condiciones generales") | — |

586	  output with this page load's field configuration, US-02-Q-17) and `plan.key`. US-03 adds

634	## 9. Non-functional requirements
635	
636	- **Accessibility (Assessment: "The wizard can be completed using only the keyboard, and fields
637	  have accessible labels"):** focus on the heading on arrival and on confirmation, description
638	  lists for data, a named focusable terms region, a labelled checkbox, a named radio group, a
639	  perceivable disabled "Pagar" with its reason, alerts announced once (AC-16, AC-17). WCAG 2.2 AA;
640	  screen reader pass at HC3.
641	- **Responsive (Assessment: "Works on mobile and desktop"):** 320–1440 CSS px without horizontal
642	  scroll; one column on narrow screens; targets ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (AC-18, manual).
643	- **Multi-country (Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and
644	  Chile"):** no terms text, field label, plan, currency, date format or masking branch per country
645	  in front-end code; dates and prices use the country's `locale` and `currencyCode` from Strapi.
646	- **Security / privacy (Assessment: "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the
647	  browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified"; "Use fictitious data only."):** one
648	  added public permission (§7.4); reads through the GET-only proxy; drafts never anonymous; no
649	  request during payment; no card data; masking at display time; no value, quote number or terms
650	  text in logs; rich text rendered without executing editor input (AC-13, AC-19). Seed and test
651	  data fictitious.
652	- **Persistence (Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not
653	  required."):** ADR-0003 unchanged; US-03 adds nothing to storage and deletes the entry on success.
654	- **Performance:** one terms request per summary entry; summary data comes from content already
655	  loaded by the guards in this page load; the price rule and masking are synchronous pure functions.
656	- **Testing (Assessment: "Unit tests for the relevant logic and at least one e2e test of the full
657	  flow for one country"):** masking, value display, quote number, terms parser and the simulated
658	  payment are unit tested; the CO full-flow e2e is completed end to end (US-03-Q-16).
659	- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, logs and docs English.

1 # FLOW — From functional user story to QA handoff 2 3 This document explains how a user story becomes a QA-ready increment in this repository: who 4 does what (AI agent or human), what each step produces, and where a person approves, rejects 5 or corrects the work. 6 7 The binding rules live in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). The agent and skill catalogue is in 8 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). 9 10 --- 11 12 ## 1. Design choices 13 14 ### Tool: Claude Code 15 16 | Need | How Claude Code covers it | 17 |---|---| 18 | Subagents with separate responsibilities, versioned | `.claude/agents/*.md`: instructions, allowed and disallowed tools, model, preloaded skills, hooks | 19 | Reusable project knowledge, versioned | `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` with templates, loaded on demand | 20 | A global context file that governs generation | `CLAUDE.md`, loaded into every session and subagent | 21 | **Enforced** (not just requested) boundaries | `PreToolUse` hooks: per-agent write scopes, a project-wide Bash guard, and permission deny rules for `.env` | 22 | Unedited session logs | JSONL transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/…` plus `/export` | 23 | Git and GitHub from the same agent | Bash with `git` and `gh`, using a repo-local identity and credential helper | 24 25 Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Codex were alternatives. We did not run a feature-by-feature 26 verification of them, so we make no claims about what they lack. Claude Code was chosen because 27 it covers every row above in one tool, from versioned files, which we verified against its 28 official documentation. The deciding capability is **per-agent tool restrictions plus lifecycle 29 hooks**: they let a human *trust* the separation of responsibilities instead of hoping for it. 30 31 ### Spec-Driven Development: our own lightweight variant 32 33 The spec is the source of truth. Tests are derived from it **before** the code, and the code 34 must make them pass. We did not adopt Spec Kit or Kiro, for three reasons: 35 36 - **Size.** Three stories do not justify their multi-phase scaffolding (constitution, plan and 37 tasks generators). 38 - **Traceability.** We need IDs that run from the story to the PR (`US-01-AC-02`, …). How control is enforced, not just requested 108 109 | Control | Mechanism | Where | 110 |---|---|---| 111 | Each agent writes only its own artifacts | `PreToolUse` hook on `Write\|Edit\|NotebookEdit` per agent (allow/deny globs, fails closed) | `.claude/agents/*.md` → `.claude/hooks/enforce-write-scope.mjs` | 112 | Developers cannot change tests; the tester cannot change code | Deny globs in the same hook | same | 113 | The reviewer cannot fix code | `Edit` disallowed; `Write` only to `reviews/US-NN-review-RN.md` | `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` | 114 | Delegation stays visible | `Agent` disallowed in every subagent (Claude Code would otherwise allow nesting up to 3 levels) | all agent files | 115 | Secrets are never read or printed | Permission deny `Read(**/.env)`, `Read(**/.env.*)` except `.env.example`; Bash guard blocks `.env` references and environment dumps | `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs` | 116 | Human checkpoints cannot be skipped by an agent | Bash guard blocks pushes to `main`, force pushes, `gh pr merge` and approvals, and `--no-verify` | `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs` | 117 | Pinned toolchain | Bash guard blocks `@angular/cli@latest` and the Angular CLI MCP server | same | 118 | The story is traceable | `scripts/trace.sh` exits non-zero on untested ACs or open blocker/major findings | `scripts/trace.sh` | 119 120 ### Known limits (accepted risks) 121 122 - **Bash can still write files.** The write-scope hooks cover the file tools, not `echo > file` 123 inside Bash. The human 126 checkpoints and GitHub branch protection (recommended for a team) remain the real controls. 127 - **Project hooks run only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted** in Claude Code. 128 129 --- 130 131 ## 5. Traceability 132 133 US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR. The IDs and conventions are in `CLAUDE.md` §9–10. 134 Example of following one thread: 135 136 ``` 137 specs/US-01/spec.md#US-01-AC-02 what must happen 138 adr/0002-…md why it is built this way 139 git log --grep US-01-AC-02 the commits that implemented it 140 frontend/**/…spec.ts › 'US-01-AC-02 …' the test that proves it 141 reviews/US-01-review-R1.md what the reviewer found, and the Resolves: commits 142 PR #N the matrix generated by scripts/trace.sh US-01 143 ``` 144 145 ## 6. Resuming between sessions 146 147 The state lives only in the repository: `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*), 148 the specs, ADRs and reviews. The `session-handoff` skill defines the start and end procedures, 149 and the end procedure includes exporting the unedited session logs to `logs/sessions/`. 150 151 --- 152 153 ## 7. Reflection 154 155 ### What we would do differently with a team of 5 developers 156 157 - **Story-level parallelism with clear ownership.** One person owns each story through the flow, 158 and the HC1/HC2 approvers rotate, so nobody approves their own spec or ADR. 159 - **Move the controls to the server.** Branch protection on `main` (required reviews, required 160 checks), CODEOWNERS for `adr/`, `.claude/` and `CLAUDE.md`, and the automated gate (step 5) 161 in CI rather than locally. Local hooks become a convenience, not the control. 162 - **Shared contracts first.** The Strapi content contract and the `FieldConfig` type would become 163 a versioned package or a generated schema, because with five people the frontend and backend 164 drift faster than one orchestrator can catch. 165 - **Changes to the flow go through PRs** with their own review. Checking the official Claude Code docs showed they can (up to 3 levels). | `Agent` is now explicitly disallowed in every subagent, and that is documented as a design decision. The guard matches command text, not intent. | Accepted as a known limit (false positives are safer than false negatives). Commit messages and PR bodies are written to files with the file tools and passed via `git commit -F` / `gh pr create --body-file`. | 180 | A widened write scope did not take effect | At HC1 the human asked for a spec annex (`seed-fields.md`). We widened the spec-writer's hook on disk and tested it (9/9 cases), but the running subagent was still blocked. Most likely Claude Code loads agent definitions, and their hooks, when the session starts. | The spec-writer staged the annex inside the spec and raised task T-30, so no silent workaround. The human chose to have the orchestrator move it mechanically, verified by diff. Rule adopted: **changes to `.claude/agents/` take effect in the next session**, so plan agent-config changes before a session, or restart after the session-handoff. | 181 | The known Bash-write limit happened in practice | In the first ADR run, the architect edited `tasks.md` through a Python script in Bash, which bypasses its write-scope hook (its Bash is read-only by definition). It declared this itself, and the orchestrator's `git diff` check confirmed the change was limited to the planned lines. | The architect was told to use Edit only on the next run, and it did. The control that caught it is the post-run diff check (`CLAUDE.md` §8), not the hook. That is why the check is mandatory. | 182 | A subagent could not write its report file | Claude Code refused to let the spike's frontend-developer write `FINDINGS.md` (a built-in rule: subagents return findings as text). The agent did not work around it; it asked the orchestrator to save the file. | The orchestrator did not do what the agent was refused, and asked the human. Decision: the findings travel **verbatim in the architect's brief**, and the architect writes `docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md` as planned. The raw text stays in the session log. | 183 | An HC2 criterion was not backed by the template | FLOW.md tells the human to read "the strongest argument against" at HC2. The architect stated it in its reports, but the ADR template had no section for it, so the ADR files lacked it. The orchestrator found this when preparing HC2 (finding H1). | The human approved H1: the `adr-madr` template and skill now require a *Strongest argument against* section, and the four ADRs got it **before** being marked Accepted, so accepted ADRs were never rewritten. | 184 | A message reached a subagent after it finished | A follow-up to the running architect (the human's "raw while editing" decision) arrived after its last step; Claude Code resumed the agent to process it. Every gate run now starts from **fresh volumes** (`docker compose -p mci-gate down -v`). The AC-03 test gained cleanup for leftovers. For a team: one isolated stack per agent, or serialise the phases that write shared data. | 188 | Unit tests were green but the real browser disagreed | 263/263 unit and component tests passed in jsdom. The first real e2e run found two defects jsdom cannot show: an unparseable number showed no message, and a late Signal Forms DOM write overwrote what the user typed. The second was **flaky**: it passed 6/6 in isolation and failed in the full suite. | The gate counts a flaky test as a failure. The orchestrator measured it (`--repeat-each`) instead of re-running until green. The developer had to prove the root cause with a deterministic reproduction and pass the full suite 3 times in a row. This is the gap SPIKE-01 had declared as unverified. | 189 | An agent fixed a security-relevant failure with bespoke code | AC-03 failed because Strapi requires read permission on a relation target. The strapi-developer made it pass with a custom create controller that relaxed the framework check, and declared it. | The orchestrator did not accept it silently and asked the human, who chose the conventional fix: widen the test token with `country.find` and revert the controller. This was recorded as ADR-0005, which **amends** ADR-0002 without rewriting it. It concluded "IPv6 `localhost`" from a test that changed **two** variables at once (explicit env vars and `127.0.0.1`). The real cause was its own command: `env $ENV npx …` in zsh, which does not word-split unquoted variables, so `E2E_BASE_URL` received the whole line. It was caught later, when the same 32-failure pattern reappeared on code that passed elsewhere. A one-variable test (Node 24 `fetch('http://localhost')` against an IPv4-only server returns 200, because `autoSelectFamily` is on) disproved the IPv6 theory. The extra `[::1]` binding (4a82769) is harmless but was not needed. The 403 regression found in the same run was real and was reproduced independently. | Corrected on the record instead of left standing. Rules adopted: **change one variable at a time** when testing a hypothesis, and run e2e only through `scripts/e2e.sh`, which sets the documented env deterministically. | 191 | A regression hid a second security bug | The same verification showed a new 403 on AC-03. Each router inherited the other's scopes, so a token with only `country.find` could also read form fields. | Fixed by giving each router fresh config objects and keeping the published-only middleware on reads only. Lesson: a failing test with an unexpected status code deserves a root cause, not a retry. Here it exposed a cross-type authorization leak that no test targeted. | 192 | The orchestrator truncated a control's output and reported a false "clean" | When exporting the US-01 logs, the orchestrator read only the last 8 lines of `scan-secrets.sh` and recorded "one scan exception". A subagent's later full scan surfaced it. | All 23 were classified by a script that never prints values. 22 are fictitious; one is a real but expired dev-admin JWT whose signing secret was destroyed, which the human accepted as an exception. The logs README carries a correction note. The first log redaction (US-01) covered the address, but missed the domain inside a subagent's plugin list, which reached `main` with PR #4. At the US-03 closure the orchestrator's redaction also missed a regex-escaped form, and every new command that named the value to check or redact was itself recorded by the transcript, in yet another escaped form. The redaction script also counted a part twice inside the full address. | A separate **personal-data policy** (human decision): secrets are rotated, personal data is redacted. `scripts/redact-logs.sh` replaces every form with `[REDACTED-PERSONAL]`, reading the values from a file outside the repository (never from a command line); counts are exact. `scan-secrets.sh`, `scan-logs.sh` and a versioned pre-commit hook block the domain by hash, so the value is not written in the repo. Git history is left as is; the human decides how to clean it before sharing. | 194 195 *(This table is extended as the stories are implemented.)* 196 197 ### Where we decided not to use AI, and why 198 199 | Point | Why not AI | 200 |---|---| 201 | H0 intake of stories (default) | The input must be the real requirement, not a model's paraphrase of it. **Exception, US-01..03:** the human (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20) asked the agent to transcribe them from the PDF. We accepted the exception because the risk (a paraphrase) is removed mechanically: the transcription is compared word by word with the `pdftotext` output of the source file (SHA-256 recorded in each `story.md`), and that comparison found 0 differences. | 202 | HC1 / HC2 / HC3 approvals and the PR merge | Accountability: the person who signs off must be a person. Agents are technically prevented from merging. | 203 | Accepting third-party skills | Supply-chain trust decision. | 204 | Step 5 automated gate | Deterministic checks are cheaper and more reliable than AI judgement, and they cannot be talked out of a failure. | 205 | Traceability matrix | Generated by `scripts/trace.sh`, so it cannot be invented. | 206 | Manual keyboard and visual QA | Real interaction quality is what automation approximates worst. | 207 | Secrets handling | No agent reads `.env`; real secrets are managed by the human. | 208 | Exporting logs with `/export` | It is a CLI command; the agent copies the raw JSONL. | 209

# FLOW — From functional user story to QA handoff This document explains how a user story becomes a QA-ready increment in this repository: who does what (AI agent or human), what each step produces, and where a person approves, rejects or corrects the work. The binding rules live in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). The agent and skill catalogue is in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). --- ## 1. Design choices ### Tool: Claude Code | Need | How Claude Code covers it | |---|---| | Subagents with separate responsibilities, versioned | `.claude/agents/*.md`: instructions, allowed and disallowed tools, model, preloaded skills, hooks | | Reusable project knowledge, versioned | `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` with templates, loaded on demand | | A global context file that governs generation | `CLAUDE.md`, loaded into every session and subagent | | **Enforced** (not just requested) boundaries | `PreToolUse` hooks: per-agent write scopes, a project-wide Bash guard, and permission deny rules for `.env` | | Unedited session logs | JSONL transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/…` plus `/export` | | Git and GitHub from the same agent | Bash with `git` and `gh`, using a repo-local identity and credential helper | Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Codex were alternatives. We did not run a feature-by-feature verification of them, so we make no claims about what they lack. Claude Code was chosen because it covers every row above in one tool, from versioned files, which we verified against its official documentation. The deciding capability is **per-agent tool restrictions plus lifecycle hooks**: they let a human *trust* the separation of responsibilities instead of hoping for it. ### Spec-Driven Development: our own lightweight variant The spec is the source of truth. Tests are derived from it **before** the code, and the code must make them pass. We did not adopt Spec Kit or Kiro, for three reasons: - **Size.** Three stories do not justify their multi-phase scaffolding (constitution, plan and tasks generators). - **Traceability.** We need IDs that run from the story to the PR (`US-01-AC-02`, …). With our own templates (`sdd-spec` skill), every artifact uses them and `scripts/trace.sh` can check them mechanically. - **Gap detection.** The evaluation rewards specs that *detect gaps in the user story*, so our spec template has a first-class **Gaps and open questions** section, where each gap carries a proposed default and a human answer. What we kept from SDD frameworks: spec → plan (ADRs + `tasks.md`) → tasks → implementation, with a human approval between spec and implementation. ### Model allocation | Role | Model | Why | |---|---|---| | Orchestrator (main session) | Claude Opus 5.5 | It holds the whole flow, talks to the human and routes the work | | spec-writer, architect | Claude Opus 5.5 | Judgement-heavy work: finding gaps, weighing alternatives, verifying facts | | test-engineer, strapi-developer, frontend-developer | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Well-scoped work guided by an approved spec, ADRs and failing tests; faster and cheaper | | code-reviewer | Claude Opus 5.5 | Deliberately a **different model from the implementers**, so the review does not share their blind spots | --- ## 2. human copies story verbatim]) --> S1[1 · Spec
spec-writer + sdd-spec] S1 --> HC1{HC1 · Spec approval
human} HC1 -- reject: feedback in Review log --> S1 HC1 -- approve --> S2[2 · ADRs
architect + adr-madr] S2 -. needs evidence .-> SP[Spike

findings by architect] SP -.-> S2 S2 --> HC2{HC2 · ADR acceptance
human} HC2 -- reject: choose another option / Rejected --> S2 HC2 -- accept --> S3[3 · Tests first, red
test-engineer + test-from-spec] S3 --> S4[4 · Implementation
strapi-developer / frontend-developer] S4 --> S5{5 · Automated gate
lint · build · unit · e2e
trace.sh · scan-secrets} S5 -- fail --> S4 S5 -- pass --> S6[6 · Code review
code-reviewer + review-checklist] S6 -- CHANGES REQUESTED --> S7[7 · Fixes
developers, Resolves: finding IDs] S7 --> S5 S6 -- APPROVED --> HC3{HC3 · PR + manual QA
human merges} HC3 -- reject: PR comments --> S7 HC3 -- merge --> QA([Ready for QA
tasks.md + logs exported]) S5 -. 3rd failure .-> ESC[[Escalate to human]] S6 -. 3rd round .-> ESC ``` --- ## 3. Step by step | Step | Description | AI used? | AI, agent, subagent or skill used | Deliverable produced | Human in the loop | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **0 · Flow setup** (once) | Repository, identity, agents, skills, hooks, scripts. Third-party skills are evaluated before adoption. | Yes | Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (main session) | `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `FLOW.md`, `.claude/**`, `scripts/**`, `docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md` | The human approves the proposal, each third-party skill (recorded decision) and the naming convention before anything is written. | | **H0 · Intake** | The story is copied **verbatim** from the assessment, so the agents start from the real input and not from a paraphrase. | **No** by default. For US-01..03: **yes**, by human decision (see below) | Default: none.
