Library facts are verified against official sources or packages. When facts are not enough, a **spike** (30–60 min, throwaway branch) produces evidence. | Yes | `architect` (Opus 5.5) + skills `adr-madr`, `strapi-content-modeling`. Spikes: `frontend-developer` (Sonnet 5.5) | `adr/NNNN-*.md` (Proposed), `adr/README.md`, `docs/spikes/SPIKE-NN-*.md` | — (next step is the gate) | | **HC2 · ADR acceptance** | Architecture is the most expensive thing to get wrong and the easiest for an agent to rationalise. | **No** | — | ADR status `Accepted` / `Rejected`, with *decision-makers* and date | **Human** reads the options and the strongest argument against the chosen one (the architect must state it). **Accept if:** the options are real, the drivers trace to requirements, the bad consequences have mitigations, and the facts are cited. **On rejection:** the human picks another option or marks it `Rejected` (the file is kept), and `architect` rewrites it. | | **3 · Tests first** | Each AC becomes a test **before** the code exists, derived from the spec and not from an implementation. The tests must fail for the right reason. | Yes | `test-engineer` (Sonnet 5.5) + skills `test-from-spec`, `dynamic-form-fields` | `*.spec.ts`, `frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts`, `tasks.md` | Orchestrator check: `trace.sh` shows a test for every non-manual AC. No human gate here, because tests are reviewed again in step 6 and at HC3. | | **4 · Implementation** | Production code that makes the tests pass, within the spec and ADRs. The write-scope hooks stop developers from editing tests or the spec. | Yes | `strapi-developer`, `frontend-developer` (Sonnet 5.5) + skills `strapi-content-modeling`, `dynamic-form-fields`, `angular-developer` (third-party, lower precedence) | `backend/**`, `frontend/**`, commits with `Refs:` | — | | **5 · Automated gate** | Deterministic checks. Neither AI judgement nor human time is spent on what a script can verify. | **No** (scripts) | lint, `ng build`, Vitest, Playwright, `docker compose up`, `scripts/trace.sh`, `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` | Command output, summarised in `tasks.md` | **On failure:** back to step 4. **On the 3rd failure** of the same story: escalate to the human. | | **6 · Code review** | An independent review against the spec, the ADRs and the checklist. The reviewer runs the checks itself and cannot modify code. | Yes | `code-reviewer` (Opus 5.5) + skill `review-checklist` | `reviews/US-NN-review-RN.md` (findings with IDs, severities, evidence) | — (findings are routed to step 7 or HC3) | | **7 · Fixes** | Each finding is fixed in a commit that references it. The next review round verifies it. | Yes | `strapi-developer` / `frontend-developer`; `test-engineer` when a finding is a missing test | Commits with `Resolves: US-NN-RN-FNN`; updated status in the next review round | **On the 3rd review round** without approval: escalate to the human. | | **HC3 · PR and manual QA** | The orchestrator opens the PR with the traceability matrix. A person checks what automation cannot: real keyboard use, visual quality, and copy in both countries. | Partly | Orchestrator opens the PR via `gh pr create`; merging is blocked for agents by a hook | GitHub PR (template + matrix), human review comments | **Human** reviews the PR and the review report, then runs the app for CO and CL, keyboard only, at mobile width. **Merge if:** the DoD (`CLAUDE.md` §12) holds and manual QA passes. **On rejection:** PR comments are turned into findings and go back to step 7. **Only the human merges.** | | **8 · QA handoff** | State and evidence are left so that QA, or a fresh session, can pick up from the repository alone. | Yes | Orchestrator + skill `session-handoff` | `tasks.md` = `Ready for QA`, `logs/sessions/*` | The human runs `/export` (a CLI command the agent cannot run) and confirms the handoff. | --- ## 4. How control is enforced, not just requested | Control | Mechanism | Where | |---|---|---| | Each agent writes only its own artifacts | `PreToolUse` hook on `Write\|Edit\|NotebookEdit` per agent (allow/deny globs, fails closed) | `.claude/agents/*.md` → `.claude/hooks/enforce-write-scope.mjs` | | Developers cannot change tests; the tester cannot change code | Deny globs in the same hook | same | | The reviewer cannot fix code | `Edit` disallowed; `Write` only to `reviews/US-NN-review-RN.md` | `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` | | Delegation stays visible | `Agent` disallowed in every subagent (Claude Code would otherwise allow nesting up to 3 levels) | all agent files | | Secrets are never read or printed | Permission deny `Read(**/.env)`, `Read(**/.env.*)` except `.env.example`; Bash guard blocks `.env` references and environment dumps | `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs` | | Human checkpoints cannot be skipped by an agent | Bash guard blocks pushes to `main`, force pushes, `gh pr merge` and approvals, and `--no-verify` | `.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs` | | Pinned toolchain | Bash guard blocks `@angular/cli@latest` and the Angular CLI MCP server | same | | The story is traceable | `scripts/trace.sh` exits non-zero on untested ACs or open blocker/major findings | `scripts/trace.sh` | ### Known limits (accepted risks) - **Bash can still write files.** The write-scope hooks cover the file tools, not `echo > file` inside Bash. Mitigation: the orchestrator checks `git diff --stat` after every subagent; the reviewer flags out-of-role changes; HC3. - **The Bash guard matches patterns.** It catches mistakes, not deliberate obfuscation. The human checkpoints and GitHub branch protection (recommended for a team) remain the real controls. - **Project hooks run only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted** in Claude Code. --- ## 5. Traceability US → spec → ADR → commit → test → review → PR. The IDs and conventions are in `CLAUDE.md` §9–10. Example of following one thread: ``` specs/US-01/spec.md#US-01-AC-02 what must happen adr/0002-…md why it is built this way git log --grep US-01-AC-02 the commits that implemented it frontend/**/…spec.ts › 'US-01-AC-02 …' the test that proves it reviews/US-01-review-R1.md what the reviewer found, and the Resolves: commits PR #N the matrix generated by scripts/trace.sh US-01 ``` ## 6. Resuming between sessions The state lives only in the repository: `specs/US-NN/tasks.md` (*Current step*, *Next action*), the specs, ADRs and reviews. The `session-handoff` skill defines the start and end procedures, and the end procedure includes exporting the unedited session logs to `logs/sessions/`. --- ## 7. Reflection ### What we would do differently with a team of 5 developers - **Story-level parallelism with clear ownership.** One person owns each story through the flow, and the HC1/HC2 approvers rotate, so nobody approves their own spec or ADR. - **Move the controls to the server.** Branch protection on `main` (required reviews, required checks), CODEOWNERS for `adr/`, `.claude/` and `CLAUDE.md`, and the automated gate (step 5) in CI rather than locally. Local hooks become a convenience, not the control. - **Shared contracts first.** The Strapi content contract and the `FieldConfig` type would become a versioned package or a generated schema, because with five people the frontend and backend drift faster than one orchestrator can catch. - **Changes to the flow go through PRs** with their own review. Changing an agent definition or a skill changes everybody's output. - **A real secret scanner** (for example, gitleaks) in pre-commit and CI, replacing our minimal script. - **Shared, short-lived sessions**: one session per story, with mandatory handoff, so that context never lives in one person's terminal. ### What did not work as expected, and how we adjusted | Issue | What happened | Adjustment | |---|---|---| | Wrong assumption about nested subagents | The initial proposal said subagents cannot spawn subagents. Checking the official Claude Code docs showed they can (up to 3 levels). | `Agent` is now explicitly disallowed in every subagent, and that is documented as a design decision. Rule adopted: facts about tools are verified before they are written down. | | A third-party skill contradicted itself | `angular-developer` says "Signal Forms MUST be used (v21+)" in one file and "prefer them, stable in v22+" in another. | We checked the Angular CHANGELOG and the published `@angular/forms@22.3.0` typings (stable since 22.0.0). The forms choice was taken away from the skill and given to an ADR after SPIKE-01, and a precedence rule was added to `CLAUDE.md`. | | `npx skills add` installs HEAD | The evaluated commit and the installed content could differ. | The skill is vendored with `git archive` at the evaluated commit, and the git tree hash is verified. | | Write-scope globs silently did not match | The first version of the hook escaped `[0-9]` character classes, so `specs/US-[0-9][0-9]/spec.md` would have blocked the spec-writer from writing its own spec. | Found by an integration test that runs the **real** frontmatter commands (30 cases). Character classes are now supported; the hook fails closed on malformed input. | | The Bash guard blocked its own author | While committing this flow, the guard blocked a heredoc that wrote a commit message, because the message *text* mentioned the skip-hooks flag. The guard matches command text, not intent. | Accepted as a known limit (false positives are safer than false negatives). Commit messages and PR bodies are written to files with the file tools and passed via `git commit -F` / `gh pr create --body-file`. | | A widened write scope did not take effect | At HC1 the human asked for a spec annex (`seed-fields.md`). We widened the spec-writer's hook on disk and tested it (9/9 cases), but the running subagent was still blocked. Most likely Claude Code loads agent definitions, and their hooks, when the session starts. | The spec-writer staged the annex inside the spec and raised task T-30, so no silent workaround. The human chose to have the orchestrator move it mechanically, verified by diff. Rule adopted: **changes to `.claude/agents/` take effect in the next session**, so plan agent-config changes before a session, or restart after the session-handoff. | | The known Bash-write limit happened in practice | In the first ADR run, the architect edited `tasks.md` through a Python script in Bash, which bypasses its write-scope hook (its Bash is read-only by definition). It declared this itself, and the orchestrator's `git diff` check confirmed the change was limited to the planned lines. | The architect was told to use Edit only on the next run, and it did. The control that caught it is the post-run diff check (`CLAUDE.md` §8), not the hook. That is why the check is mandatory. | | A subagent could not write its report file | Claude Code refused to let the spike's frontend-developer write `FINDINGS.md` (a built-in rule: subagents return findings as text). The agent did not work around it; it asked the orchestrator to save the file. | The orchestrator did not do what the agent was refused, and asked the human. Decision: the findings travel **verbatim in the architect's brief**, and the architect writes `docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md` as planned. The raw text stays in the session log. | | An HC2 criterion was not backed by the template | FLOW.md tells the human to read "the strongest argument against" at HC2. The architect stated it in its reports, but the ADR template had no section for it, so the ADR files lacked it. The orchestrator found this when preparing HC2 (finding H1). | The human approved H1: the `adr-madr` template and skill now require a *Strongest argument against* section, and the four ADRs got it **before** being marked Accepted, so accepted ADRs were never rewritten. | | A message reached a subagent after it finished | A follow-up to the running architect (the human's "raw while editing" decision) arrived after its last step; Claude Code resumed the agent to process it. The orchestrator checked the file instead of trusting the first report. | Rule adopted: after messaging a running subagent, verify the file effect before advancing the gate. | | A subagent's stray background process delayed its replies | In step 3 the test-engineer left a background shell running `cat` with no input. Claude Code held its follow-up replies until that background work ended, so for several minutes the orchestrator could not get the agent's answers. | The orchestrator verified the effects in the files instead of waiting, confirmed the process wrote nothing, and stopped it (`kill`). Briefs now say "do not start any background command". | | The secret scanner had no way to accept a justified false positive | The scanner flagged fictitious values in tests (a fake bearer token for a negative test, throwaway Strapi secrets). The rule "do not commit; report to the human" worked, but the only fixes were editing the scanner ad hoc or weakening the test data. | Human decision: an explicit, justified marker on the same line, `scan-secrets: allow ()`. A marker without a reason does not count. The scanner lists and counts every exception, and the review checklist requires confirming each one. | | Parallel agents polluted a shared environment | During the gate-1 fixes, the strapi-developer reproduced the AC-03 400 by creating a debug field (`dbgfield`, label "X") with no teardown in the shared gate Strapi. That broke AC-01 for the other two agents, who reported it rather than "fixing" it. | The orchestrator traced it (anonymous field list), and the owner removed it along with its tokens. Every gate run now starts from **fresh volumes** (`docker compose -p mci-gate down -v`). The AC-03 test gained cleanup for leftovers. For a team: one isolated stack per agent, or serialise the phases that write shared data. | | Unit tests were green but the real browser disagreed | 263/263 unit and component tests passed in jsdom. The first real e2e run found two defects jsdom cannot show: an unparseable number showed no message, and a late Signal Forms DOM write overwrote what the user typed. The second was **flaky**: it passed 6/6 in isolation and failed in the full suite. | The gate counts a flaky test as a failure. The orchestrator measured it (`--repeat-each`) instead of re-running until green. The developer had to prove the root cause with a deterministic reproduction and pass the full suite 3 times in a row. This is the gap SPIKE-01 had declared as unverified. | | An agent fixed a security-relevant failure with bespoke code | AC-03 failed because Strapi requires read permission on a relation target. The strapi-developer made it pass with a custom create controller that relaxed the framework check, and declared it. | The orchestrator did not accept it silently and asked the human, who chose the conventional fix: widen the test token with `country.find` and revert the controller. This was recorded as ADR-0005, which **amends** ADR-0002 without rewriting it. The architect's write-up also corrected an orchestrator claim ("exposes nothing new") that was not fully true. | | The orchestrator misdiagnosed its own shell bug as a product regression | After review fix F07 (Strapi port on `127.0.0.1` only), the orchestrator's e2e run showed 32 failures. It concluded "IPv6 `localhost`" from a test that changed **two** variables at once (explicit env vars and `127.0.0.1`). The real cause was its own command: `env $ENV npx …` in zsh, which does not word-split unquoted variables, so `E2E_BASE_URL` received the whole line. It was caught later, when the same 32-failure pattern reappeared on code that passed elsewhere. A one-variable test (Node 24 `fetch('http://localhost')` against an IPv4-only server returns 200, because `autoSelectFamily` is on) disproved the IPv6 theory. The extra `[::1]` binding (4a82769) is harmless but was not needed. The 403 regression found in the same run was real and was reproduced independently. | Corrected on the record instead of left standing. Rules adopted: **change one variable at a time** when testing a hypothesis, and run e2e only through `scripts/e2e.sh`, which sets the documented env deterministically. | | A regression hid a second security bug | The same verification showed a new 403 on AC-03. The root cause was not the relation rule: the two content routers shared one module-level route-config object, which Strapi mutates in place when it assigns scopes. Each router inherited the other's scopes, so a token with only `country.find` could also read form fields. | Fixed by giving each router fresh config objects and keeping the published-only middleware on reads only. Lesson: a failing test with an unexpected status code deserves a root cause, not a retry. Here it exposed a cross-type authorization leak that no test targeted. | | The orchestrator truncated a control's output and reported a false "clean" | When exporting the US-01 logs, the orchestrator read only the last 8 lines of `scan-secrets.sh` and recorded "one scan exception". The scan had **23** unmarked findings. The logs were merged to `main` in PR #4 with that wrong record. A subagent's later full scan surfaced it. | All 23 were classified by a script that never prints values. 22 are fictitious; one is a real but expired dev-admin JWT whose signing secret was destroyed, which the human accepted as an exception. The logs README carries a correction note. Rules adopted: **never truncate the output of a control** (no `tail`/`head` on scanners, test runners or gates), and the number of findings must match the number recorded before a log is committed (`session-handoff`). | | Personal data kept reappearing in the logs | Claude Code injects the human's account e-mail into every session's context, so every transcript contains it. The first log redaction (US-01) covered the address, but missed the domain inside a subagent's plugin list, which reached `main` with PR #4. At the US-03 closure the orchestrator's redaction also missed a regex-escaped form, and every new command that named the value to check or redact was itself recorded by the transcript, in yet another escaped form. The redaction script also counted a part twice inside the full address. | A separate **personal-data policy** (human decision): secrets are rotated, personal data is redacted. `scripts/redact-logs.sh` replaces every form with `[REDACTED-PERSONAL]`, reading the values from a file outside the repository (never from a command line); counts are exact. `scan-secrets.sh`, `scan-logs.sh` and a versioned pre-commit hook block the domain by hash, so the value is not written in the repo. Git history is left as is; the human decides how to clean it before sharing. | *(This table is extended as the stories are implemented.)* ### Where we decided not to use AI, and why | Point | Why not AI | |---|---| | H0 intake of stories (default) | The input must be the real requirement, not a model's paraphrase of it. **Exception, US-01..03:** the human (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20) asked the agent to transcribe them from the PDF. We accepted the exception because the risk (a paraphrase) is removed mechanically: the transcription is compared word by word with the `pdftotext` output of the source file (SHA-256 recorded in each `story.md`), and that comparison found 0 differences. | | HC1 / HC2 / HC3 approvals and the PR merge | Accountability: the person who signs off must be a person. Agents are technically prevented from merging. | | Accepting third-party skills | Supply-chain trust decision. | | Step 5 automated gate | Deterministic checks are cheaper and more reliable than AI judgement, and they cannot be talked out of a failure. | | Traceability matrix | Generated by `scripts/trace.sh`, so it cannot be invented. | | Manual keyboard and visual QA | Real interaction quality is what automation approximates worst. | | Secrets handling | No agent reads `.env`; real secrets are managed by the human. | | Exporting logs with `/export` | It is a CLI command; the agent copies the raw JSONL. |

Design choices 13 14 ### Tool: Claude Code 15 16 | Need | How Claude Code covers it | 17 |---|---| 18 | Subagents with separate responsibilities, versioned | `.claude/agents/*.md`: instructions, allowed and disallowed tools, model, preloaded skills, hooks | 19 | Reusable project knowledge, versioned | `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` with templates, loaded on demand | 20 | A global context file that governs generation | `CLAUDE.md`, loaded into every session and subagent | 21 | **Enforced** (not just requested) boundaries | `PreToolUse` hooks: per-agent write scopes, a project-wide Bash guard, and permission deny rules for `.env` | 22 | Unedited session logs | JSONL transcripts in `~/.claude/projects/…` plus `/export` | 23 | Git and GitHub from the same agent | Bash with `git` and `gh`, using a repo-local identity and credential helper | 24 25 Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Codex were alternatives. We did not run a feature-by-feature 26 verification of them, so we make no claims about what they lack. Claude Code was chosen because 27 it covers every row above in one tool, from versioned files, which we verified against its 28 official documentation. The deciding capability is **per-agent tool restrictions plus lifecycle 29 hooks**: they let a human *trust* the separation of responsibilities instead of hoping for it. 30 31 ### Spec-Driven Development: our own lightweight variant 32 33 The spec is the source of truth. Tests are derived from it **before** the code, and the code 34 must make them pass. We did not adopt Spec Kit or Kiro, for three reasons: 35 36 - **Size.** Three stories do not justify their multi-phase scaffolding (constitution, plan and 37 tasks generators). 38 - **Traceability.** We need IDs that run from the story to the PR (`US-01-AC-02`, …). With our 39 own templates (`sdd-spec` skill), every artifact uses them and `scripts/trace.sh` can check 40 them mechanically. 41 - **Gap detection.** The evaluation rewards specs that *detect gaps in the user story*, so our 42 spec template has a first-class **Gaps and open questions** section, where each gap carries a 43 proposed default and a human answer. 44 45 What we kept from SDD frameworks: spec → plan (ADRs + `tasks.md`) → tasks → implementation, with 46 a human approval between spec and implementation. 47 48 ### Model allocation 49 50 | Role | Model | Why | 51 |---|---|---| 52 | Orchestrator (main session) | Claude Opus 5.5 | It holds the whole flow, talks to the human and routes the work | 53 | spec-writer, architect | Claude Opus 5.5 | Judgement-heavy work: finding gaps, weighing alternatives, verifying facts | 54 | test-engineer, strapi-developer, frontend-developer | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Well-scoped work guided by an approved spec, ADRs and failing tests; faster and cheaper | 55 | code-reviewer | Claude Opus 5.5 | Deliberately a **different model from the implementers**, so the review does not share their blind spots | 56 57 --- 58 59 ## 2. Local hooks become a convenience, not the control. 162 - **Shared contracts first.** The Strapi content contract and the `FieldConfig` type would become 163 a versioned package or a generated schema, because with five people the frontend and backend 164 drift faster than one orchestrator can catch. 165 - **Changes to the flow go through PRs** with their own review. Changing an agent definition or 166 a skill changes everybody's output. 167 - **A real secret scanner** (for example, gitleaks) in pre-commit and CI, replacing our minimal script. 168 - **Shared, short-lived sessions**: one session per story, with mandatory handoff, so that 169 context never lives in one person's terminal. 170 171 ### What did not work as expected, and how we adjusted 172 173 | Issue | What happened | Adjustment | 174 |---|---|---| 175 | Wrong assumption about nested subagents | The initial proposal said subagents cannot spawn subagents. 9	# ADR-0004: Forms library for the Strapi-driven step 1 form
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	Step 1 of the wizard (US-01) is a form whose fields, order, options, rules and Spanish copy all
14	come from Strapi at runtime (`specs/US-01/spec.md` §7.1, BR-01, BR-06). The field set is only
15	known after the configuration is fetched, so the form model is built at runtime. `CLAUDE.md` §7
16	blocks production form code until an ADR picks the forms approach, and `CLAUDE.md` §5 says the
17	vendored `angular-developer` skill's "You MUST use Angular's new Signal Forms API" is not
18	binding. SPIKE-01 built the same form twice, with Signal Forms and with Reactive Forms
19	(`FormRecord`), over a shared library-agnostic validation core. This ADR decides which approach
20	the production step 1 uses, and which parts stay outside the library.
21	
22	## Decision Drivers
23	
24	- **D1. Dynamic form with typed validations.** "Step 1 form generated dynamically from the
25	  Strapi configuration, with typed validations" (assessment); spec §9 *Typed validations*
26	  (configuration parsed at the boundary into a typed model; validators are pure functions with an
27	  injectable clock).
28	- **D2. Angular 21+ idioms.** "Angular 21 or later: standalone components, signals, built-in
29	  control flow (@if, @for), no NgModules" (assessment). Angular is pinned to **22.3.0**
30	  (`CLAUDE.md` §4).
31	- **D3. Error visibility and focus.** Errors appear after blur or after a failed "Continuar",
32	  update while typing once shown, and focus moves to the first invalid field in `sortOrder`
33	  (US-01-AC-10, US-01-Q-13).
34	- **D4. Hydration and pruning.** The form shows stored values on entry with no errors
35	  (US-01-AC-04, AC-20, AC-21); values of keys no longer configured are dropped and stale select
36	  values cleared (US-01-AC-23, Q-16).
37	- **D5. Correct empty and number semantics.** Required vs empty (`0` is a value, `''` is empty),
38	  integer-only numbers (US-01-AC-05, AC-08, Q-12, Q-26).
39	- **D6. Output shape.** Step 1 hands values to later steps in the §7.3 shape: trimmed text,
40	  integers, ISO dates, booleans, and `null` for an empty optional field.
41	- **D7. Accessibility.** Native controls, accessible name, description, required and invalid
42	  states, error announced once (US-01-AC-25, spec §9).
43	- **D8. Risk and reversibility.** Library maturity, amount of custom code, and the cost of
44	  switching later (`adr-madr`: hard-to-reverse decisions).
45	
46	## Considered Options
47	
48	1. **Signal Forms** (`@angular/forms/signals`: `form`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `validate`,
49	   `submit`) over the shared validation core.
50	2. **Reactive Forms** (`FormRecord<FormControl<…>>` with `ReactiveFormsModule`) over the same
51	   core.
52	3. **No forms library**: native inputs bound to plain signals (`[value]` / `(input)` /
53	   `(blur)`), with validation, touched state, submit and focus handled by the shared core and the
54	   component.
55	
56	## Decision Outcome
57	
58	Chosen option: **"Signal Forms over the shared validation core"**. Both libraries met every
59	SPIKE-01 criterion (11/11 each). The tie-breakers are D2, D3 and D5. Signal Forms keeps state in
60	signals with no bridges. `submit()` touches every field and `focusBoundControl()` moves focus
61	(D3), so neither needs a DOM lookup or an extra call. With a string model, number inputs had no
62	accessor surprises (D5). The Reactive Forms adapter needed `normalise()` to fix a real
63	functional bug: `NumberValueAccessor` wrote a number into a control declared as string, and a
64	valid year was read as empty. Its one typing advantage (no casts in templates) does not help D1,
65	because the typed contract lives in the parsed `FieldConfig` and the pure validators, not in
66	the form model.
67	
68	### What is decided
69	
70	- **Library and version:** `@angular/forms/signals` from `@angular/forms` 22.3.0 (pinned, as all
71	  `@angular/*`, by `CLAUDE.md` §4). The step 1 page does not import `ReactiveFormsModule`,
72	  `FormControl`, `FormGroup`, `FormRecord` or `@angular/forms/signals-compat`.
73	- **Validation stays in the core, not in the library.** Validation and message resolution are
74	  pure functions in `field-validators.ts` (`CLAUDE.md` §6). They import nothing from
75	  `@angular/forms` and get "today" from the injectable clock (US-01-Q-06). Each field gets
76	  exactly one `validate()` that calls the shared function and returns
77	  `{ kind: 'custom', message }`. Signal Forms built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
78	  `pattern()`, …) are not used. The rule order, the empty-optional skip (Q-26) and the message
79	  priority (Q-04) are configuration semantics, and keeping them in one function keeps this
80	  decision reversible (D8).
81	- **Editing model:** `Record<string, string | boolean>`. `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`
82	  hold strings (`''` = empty); `checkbox` holds a boolean. The model never holds `null`. This
83	  deliberately differs from the vendored skill's "use `0` for numbers": `0` is a valid value, so
84	  it cannot mean empty (D5, AC-08). `number` fields use a native `<input type="number">` bound to
85	  the string model, and integer-only is a validator rule (Q-12).
86	- **Output mapping:** the §7.3 values come from a pure `toOutput(configs, model)`: trimmed text,
87	  integer, option value, ISO date, boolean, and `null` for an empty optional field. The output is
88	  never read back into the form model; hydration goes through `hydrate()`.
89	- **Hydration and pruning:** the model is created from `hydrate(configs, storedValues)`, which
90	  keeps only configured keys and converts stored values to the editing model, **before** `form()`
91	  is called. Signal Forms does not drop unknown keys by itself (SPIKE-01 row g). Clearing a stale
92	  select value and writing the pruned state back belong to the store (ADR-0003).
93	- **Lifecycle:** the form is built once per configuration load, in the injection context of the
94	  component that owns it (a field initialiser of a form component created when the configuration
95	  is ready). `form()` is not called inside `computed()`, because it creates an effect
96	  (`NG0602`). A different configuration (another country) means a new component instance, not a
97	  rebuilt form inside a live one.
98	- **Error visibility:** an error is shown when `touched() && invalid()`, and only the first
99	  message (the core already resolves one message per field). "Continuar" calls `submit()` (or
100	  uses `FormRoot` with `submission` options). `submit()` marks every field as touched.
101	- **Focus on a failed attempt:** in `onInvalid`, focus the first invalid field in the
102	  configuration's `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`.
103	- **Typing at the template boundary:** the runtime union `string | boolean` does not compile
104	  against native controls (SPIKE-01, *Typing*). Two narrowing accessors (`FieldTree<string>`
105	  and `FieldTree<boolean>`), selected by the field `type` in a static `@switch`, are the only
106	  casts allowed. They live in the step 1 form component and nowhere else.
107	- **Accessibility attributes** (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required`, error
108	  element) are bound explicitly in the template, as in the spike. `provideSignalFormsConfig` is
109	  not relied on unless a later review shows it covers AC-25.
110	
111	### Consequences
112	
113	- Good, because the form state is signals end to end (D2): `valid()`, `touched()`, `errors()`
114	  feed the template and the wizard store with no `toSignal` or `valueChanges` bridges.
115	- Good, because blur and failed-submit visibility share one condition, and focus uses a library
116	  API instead of DOM queries by id (D3). The spike's sensitivity check proves the test catches its
117	  removal.
118	- Good, because the string editing model avoids the accessor writing `number | null` into a
119	  string-typed state (D5). Integer-only and required-vs-empty stay explicit, testable rules.
120	- Good, because the validation core is library-agnostic (209 lines in the spike) and is
121	  unit-tested without Angular forms. Switching library later means rewriting one adapter of
122	  about 110 lines plus its template, not the rules (D8).
123	- Bad, because Signal Forms has been public API only since **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, about five
124	  and a half months, and the `forms` scope has had **39** fix, perf or feat entries between
125	  22.0.0 and 22.3.0 in the CHANGELOG. Mitigation: pinned 22.3.0; the parts we use are small
126	  (`form`, `validate`, `submit`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `focusBoundControl`), all
127	  `@publicApi 22.0`; no async validators, no `debounce`, no `hidden`/`disabled` logic; validation
128	  semantics live outside the library.
129	- Bad, because the runtime model loses static typing in templates and needs two casts. A cast
130	  cannot catch a mismatch between a field's `type` and the accessor used. Mitigation: the
131	  accessor is picked in the same `@switch` branch that renders the control; a component test
132	  renders every field type and asserts the DOM value, and the review checklist rejects other
133	  casts on form fields.
134	- Bad, because an unknown key on the field tree compiles but throws at runtime
135	  (`TypeError: f.<key> is not a function`). Mitigation: the template iterates only over the
136	  parsed configuration, from which the model is built; no code indexes the tree by a literal key.
137	- Bad, because all SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom: real focus, native date and number UI,
138	  `badInput` and screen reader announcements are unverified. Under the HTML value sanitisation
139	  rule for `type=number`, unparseable input such as `1e` makes `element.value` `''`, so it
140	  would show the "required" message rather than the format message. The spike did not exercise
141	  this. Mitigation: the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) exercises keyboard and
142	  validation in a real browser; the HC3 manual pass includes a screen reader check (spec §9).
143	- Neutral: Reactive Forms remains fully supported in 22.3.0 (`FormRecord` and
144	  `ReactiveFormsModule` are `@publicApi`, not deprecated). Later stories may revisit if a form
145	  needs something Signal Forms lacks.
146	
147	### Strongest argument against
148	
149	Signal Forms has been public API only since 22.0.0, about five and a half months, with 39
150	forms-scope fix, perf or feat entries through 22.3.0. All SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom, not
151	a real browser. For a form built at runtime its typing benefit largely disappears: the template
152	needed casts, and an unknown key compiles but throws at runtime. Reactive Forms `FormRecord` is
153	the long-established path for runtime-keyed forms; in the spike it compiled with no casts, and
154	`setValue` throws on stale keys.
155	
156	**Why we accept it:** only APIs tagged `@publicApi 22.0` are used, with no async validators,
157	`debounce` or `hidden`/`disabled` logic, on a pinned 22.3.0. Validation semantics live outside
158	the library, so switching to Reactive Forms means rewriting one adapter of about 110 lines plus
159	its template, not the rules (D8). The Reactive adapter was not free of risk either: it needed
160	`normalise()` to fix a real bug where `NumberValueAccessor` wrote `number | null` into a
161	string-typed control (D5). The real-browser gap is covered by the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) and the
162	HC3 screen reader check.
163	
164	### Confirmation
165	
166	- **Tests (test-engineer, step 3):** component tests in `quote-form-page.spec.ts` for
167	  US-01-AC-10 (no errors on entry; error after blur; all errors and focus on the first invalid
168	  field in `sortOrder` after a failed "Continuar", checked through `document.activeElement`),
169	  US-01-AC-04 / AC-23 (hydrated values shown, pristine, stale key dropped, stale select shows the
170	  prompt) and US-01-AC-05 (`2015.5` invalid). Unit tests of `toOutput` for every §7.3 mapping.

  values cleared (US-01-AC-23, Q-16).
- **D5. Correct empty and number semantics.** Required vs empty (`0` is a value, `''` is empty),
  integer-only numbers (US-01-AC-05, AC-08, Q-12, Q-26).
- **D6. Output shape.** Step 1 hands values to later steps in the §7.3 shape: trimmed text,
  integers, ISO dates, booleans, and `null` for an empty optional field.
- **D7. Accessibility.** Native controls, accessible name, description, required and invalid
  states, error announced once (US-01-AC-25, spec §9).
- **D8. Risk and reversibility.** Library maturity, amount of custom code, and the cost of
  switching later (`adr-madr`: hard-to-reverse decisions).

## Considered Options

1. **Signal Forms** (`@angular/forms/signals`: `form`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `validate`,
   `submit`) over the shared validation core.
2. **Reactive Forms** (`FormRecord<FormControl<…>>` with `ReactiveFormsModule`) over the same
   core.
3. **No forms library**: native inputs bound to plain signals (`[value]` / `(input)` /
   `(blur)`), with validation, touched state, submit and focus handled by the shared core and the
   component.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"Signal Forms over the shared validation core"**. Both libraries met every
SPIKE-01 criterion (11/11 each). The tie-breakers are D2, D3 and D5. Signal Forms keeps state in
signals with no bridges. `submit()` touches every field and `focusBoundControl()` moves focus
(D3), so neither needs a DOM lookup or an extra call. With a string model, number inputs had no
accessor surprises (D5). The Reactive Forms adapter needed `normalise()` to fix a real
functional bug: `NumberValueAccessor` wrote a number into a control declared as string, and a
valid year was read as empty. Its one typing advantage (no casts in templates) does not help D1,
because the typed contract lives in the parsed `FieldConfig` and the pure validators, not in
the form model.

### What is decided

- **Library and version:** `@angular/forms/signals` from `@angular/forms` 22.3.0 (pinned, as all
  `@angular/*`, by `CLAUDE.md` §4). The step 1 page does not import `ReactiveFormsModule`,
  `FormControl`, `FormGroup`, `FormRecord` or `@angular/forms/signals-compat`.
- **Validation stays in the core, not in the library.** Validation and message resolution are
  pure functions in `field-validators.ts` (`CLAUDE.md` §6). They import nothing from
  `@angular/forms` and get "today" from the injectable clock (US-01-Q-06). Each field gets
  exactly one `validate()` that calls the shared function and returns
  `{ kind: 'custom', message }`. Signal Forms built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
  `pattern()`, …) are not used. The rule order, the empty-optional skip (Q-26) and the message
  priority (Q-04) are configuration semantics, and keeping them in one function keeps this
  decision reversible (D8).
- **Editing model:** `Record<string, string | boolean>`. `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`
  hold strings (`''` = empty); `checkbox` holds a boolean. The model never holds `null`. This
  deliberately differs from the vendored skill's "use `0` for numbers": `0` is a valid value, so
  it cannot mean empty (D5, AC-08). `number` fields use a native `<input type="number">` bound to
  the string model, and integer-only is a validator rule (Q-12).
- **Output mapping:** the §7.3 values come from a pure `toOutput(configs, model)`: trimmed text,
  integer, option value, ISO date, boolean, and `null` for an empty optional field. The output is
  never read back into the form model; hydration goes through `hydrate()`.
- **Hydration and pruning:** the model is created from `hydrate(configs, storedValues)`, which
  keeps only configured keys and converts stored values to the editing model, **before** `form()`
  is called. Signal Forms does not drop unknown keys by itself (SPIKE-01 row g). Clearing a stale
  select value and writing the pruned state back belong to the store (ADR-0003).
- **Lifecycle:** the form is built once per configuration load, in the injection context of the
  component that owns it (a field initialiser of a form component created when the configuration
  is ready). `form()` is not called inside `computed()`, because it creates an effect
  (`NG0602`). A different configuration (another country) means a new component instance, not a
  rebuilt form inside a live one.
- **Error visibility:** an error is shown when `touched() && invalid()`, and only the first
  message (the core already resolves one message per field). "Continuar" calls `submit()` (or
  uses `FormRoot` with `submission` options). `submit()` marks every field as touched.
- **Focus on a failed attempt:** in `onInvalid`, focus the first invalid field in the
  configuration's `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`.
- **Typing at the template boundary:** the runtime union `string | boolean` does not compile
  against native controls (SPIKE-01, *Typing*). Two narrowing accessors (`FieldTree<string>`
  and `FieldTree<boolean>`), selected by the field `type` in a static `@switch`, are the only
  casts allowed. They live in the step 1 form component and nowhere else.
- **Accessibility attributes** (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required`, error
  element) are bound explicitly in the template, as in the spike. `provideSignalFormsConfig` is
  not relied on unless a later review shows it covers AC-25.

### Consequences

- Good, because the form state is signals end to end (D2): `valid()`, `touched()`, `errors()`
  feed the template and the wizard store with no `toSignal` or `valueChanges` bridges.
- Good, because blur and failed-submit visibility share one condition, and focus uses a library
  API instead of DOM queries by id (D3). The spike's sensitivity check proves the test catches its
  removal.
- Good, because the string editing model avoids the accessor writing `number | null` into a
  string-typed state (D5). Integer-only and required-vs-empty stay explicit, testable rules.
- Good, because the validation core is library-agnostic (209 lines in the spike) and is
  unit-tested without Angular forms. Switching library later means rewriting one adapter of
  about 110 lines plus its template, not the rules (D8).
- Bad, because Signal Forms has been public API only since **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, about five
  and a half months, and the `forms` scope has had **39** fix, perf or feat entries between
  22.0.0 and 22.3.0 in the CHANGELOG. Mitigation: pinned 22.3.0; the parts we use are small
  (`form`, `validate`, `submit`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `focusBoundControl`), all
  `@publicApi 22.0`; no async validators, no `debounce`, no `hidden`/`disabled` logic; validation
  semantics live outside the library.
- Bad, because the runtime model loses static typing in templates and needs two casts. A cast
  cannot catch a mismatch between a field's `type` and the accessor used. Mitigation: the
  accessor is picked in the same `@switch` branch that renders the control; a component test
  renders every field type and asserts the DOM value, and the review checklist rejects other
  casts on form fields.
- Bad, because an unknown key on the field tree compiles but throws at runtime
  (`TypeError: f.<key> is not a function`). Mitigation: the template iterates only over the
  parsed configuration, from which the model is built; no code indexes the tree by a literal key.
- Bad, because all SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom: real focus, native date and number UI,
  `badInput` and screen reader announcements are unverified. Under the HTML value sanitisation
  rule for `type=number`, unparseable input such as `1e` makes `element.value` `''`, so it
  would show the "required" message rather than the format message. The spike did not exercise
  this. Mitigation: the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) exercises keyboard and
  validation in a real browser; the HC3 manual pass includes a screen reader check (spec §9).
- Neutral: Reactive Forms remains fully supported in 22.3.0 (`FormRecord` and
  `ReactiveFormsModule` are `@publicApi`, not deprecated). Later stories may revisit if a form
  needs something Signal Forms lacks.

### Strongest argument against

Signal Forms has been public API only since 22.0.0, about five and a half months, with 39
forms-scope fix, perf or feat entries through 22.3.0. All SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom, not
a real browser. For a form built at runtime its typing benefit largely disappears: the template
needed casts, and an unknown key compiles but throws at runtime. Reactive Forms `FormRecord` is
the long-established path for runtime-keyed forms; in the spike it compiled with no casts, and
`setValue` throws on stale keys.

**Why we accept it:** only APIs tagged `@publicApi 22.0` are used, with no async validators,
`debounce` or `hidden`/`disabled` logic, on a pinned 22.3.0. Validation semantics live outside
the library, so switching to Reactive Forms means rewriting one adapter of about 110 lines plus
its template, not the rules (D8). The Reactive adapter was not free of risk either: it needed
`normalise()` to fix a real bug where `NumberValueAccessor` wrote `number | null` into a
string-typed control (D5). The real-browser gap is covered by the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) and the
HC3 screen reader check.

### Confirmation

- **Tests (test-engineer, step 3):** component tests in `quote-form-page.spec.ts` for
  US-01-AC-10 (no errors on entry; error after blur; all errors and focus on the first invalid
  field in `sortOrder` after a failed "Continuar", checked through `document.activeElement`),
  US-01-AC-04 / AC-23 (hydrated values shown, pristine, stale key dropped, stale select shows the
  prompt) and US-01-AC-05 (`2015.5` invalid). Unit tests of `toOutput` for every §7.3 mapping.

105	## 4. Business rules
106	
107	| ID | Original (source) | Refined (precise, testable) | Covered by |
108	|---|---|---|---|
109	| US-01-BR-01 | Story: "Each field is configured in Strapi with: label, type (text, number, select, date, checkbox), required flag, validations, help text, error message, order and country." | Each field configuration has: `key` (required, unique per country, see §7.1), `label` (required, non-empty), `type` (exactly one of `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`), `isRequired` (boolean), `rules` (zero or more structured validation rules of the kinds in §7.1), `helpText` (optional), `errorMessage` (required, field level, used for any failure without a rule-specific message, US-01-Q-04), optional rule-specific messages, `sortOrder` (integer) and country. Only **published** configurations of the current country are rendered, sorted by `sortOrder` ascending; ties are broken by `key` ascending. A configuration that fails boundary validation is not rendered (US-01-Q-18). An empty optional field passes every rule; rules run only on non-empty values (US-01-Q-26). A `number` or `date` input whose text the browser cannot read (`validity.badInput`; for example `1e` in a number, or a partly cleared date) is not an empty optional field: it is invalid whether it is required or optional (v0.5, US-01-R3-F01; AC-09). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-02, US-01-AC-08, US-01-AC-09, US-01-AC-10, US-01-AC-14, US-01-AC-16 |
110	| US-01-BR-02 | Story: "Select fields (for example, make or city) get their options from Strapi." | A `select` field shows exactly the options configured for it in Strapi, each with `value` and `label`, in `sortOrder` ascending. No option is pre-selected; the first entry is a non-selectable prompt "Selecciona una opción" (code-owned copy, US-01-Q-14). A `select` with zero options is invalid configuration and is not rendered. The stored value is the option `value`, not its label. | US-01-AC-07, US-01-AC-14, US-01-AC-23 |
111	| US-01-BR-03 | Story: "The vehicle year cannot be later than next year or more than 20 years old." | With `Y` = the calendar year of *today*, a vehicle year `v` is valid if and only if `v` is an integer and `Y − 20 ≤ v ≤ Y + 1` (both limits inclusive). On 2026-11-20 the valid range is 2006–2027. The limits 20 and 1 are parameters of the `yearRange` rule in the configuration (seeded as 20 and 1 for both countries), so the business can change them (US-01-Q-05). | US-01-AC-05 |
112	| US-01-BR-04 | Story: "The policyholder must be of legal age." | The birth date is valid if and only if the age in completed years on *today* is ≥ the configured `minAge` (seeded as 18 for CO and for CL). A person turns N on the anniversary of their birth date; for a 29 February birth date, in non-leap years the anniversary is 1 March (US-01-Q-07). Birth dates after today are invalid. | US-01-AC-06 |
113	| US-01-BR-05 | Story context: "In Colombia the identity document is usually the citizenship ID (cédula de ciudadanía) or foreigner ID (cédula de extranjería), and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (placa). In Chile the document is the RUT and the vehicle is identified by its license plate (patente)." | CO step 1 includes a document type select with options CC "Cédula de ciudadanía" and CE "Cédula de extranjería", a document number (digits only, 6–10) and a plate labelled "Placa" (3 letters + 3 digits). CL step 1 includes a document number labelled "RUT" (with or without dots and dash, check digit `0–9`/`K`, check digit verified per US-01-Q-09) and a plate labelled "Patente" (2 letters + 4 digits, or 4 letters + 2 digits). CL has no document type field. These are **seed content**, not code; the seed is summarised in §7.2 and listed in full in the annex [seed-fields.md](seed-fields.md) (US-01-Q-03). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-11, US-01-AC-12 |
114	| US-01-BR-06 | Story context: "The business team wants to add, remove or reorder fields from Strapi without asking development for changes." Assessment: "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." | Publishing, unpublishing or editing a field configuration (including its order, options, rules and copy) is reflected in step 1 on the next full page load of the app, with no code change, build or deployment. No browser-side or proxy cache may delay this beyond that reload (US-01-Q-16). Unpublished (draft) changes are never shown, and no anonymous caller (glossary: any request Strapi does not authenticate, whatever its headers or path letter case) can read them, not even by asking the content API for `status=draft` (ADR-0002). | US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-AC-23, US-01-AC-28 |
115	| US-01-BR-07 | Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." Business context: "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy, so the content the app consumes changes by country." | One production build serves both countries. The supported countries are the published `country` entries in Strapi, loaded once per full page load (ADR-0001); no country code, country name or country list exists in front-end code. The country context selects which content is loaded; no country-specific branch, field list or copy exists in front-end code (wizard chrome copy excepted, US-01-Q-14; the complete list is §8.1). A country code that is not in the loaded list shows the unknown-country state and loads no form. If the country list cannot be loaded, the root chooser and the unknown-country page show a load error with "Reintentar", never "Este país no está disponible." (ADR-0001). Data entered in one country context is never shown in the other (US-01-Q-02). | US-01-AC-01, US-01-AC-17, US-01-AC-22 |
116	| US-01-BR-08 | Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." Story AC "Keep data when going back". | Step 1 values stay in the browser: they are held in the wizard state on the front end and never sent to Strapi or any other server. They survive moving between steps (in-app and browser navigation) and a reload in the same tab; they are kept in `sessionStorage` for one country and cleared when the tab closes, when another country's context is entered and after a successful payment (ADR-0003). The store keeps the raw editing values and writes them on every change, so a reload restores exactly what was typed, valid or not (ADR-0003, HC2). Step 1 hands its values to the next steps only through the wizard state, as the typed output of §7.3, which is produced only on a valid "Continuar". | US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-18, US-01-AC-20, US-01-AC-21, US-01-AC-27 |

1073	## 9. Non-functional requirements
1074	
1075	- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
1076	  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
1077	  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
1078	  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
1079	  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
1080	- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
1081	  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
1082	  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
1083	- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
1084	  fields or copy (BR-07).
1085	- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
1086	  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
1087	- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
1088	  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
1089	- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
1090	  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
1091	  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
1092	  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
1093	  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
1094	  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
1095	- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
1096	  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
1097	  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
1098	- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
1099	  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
1100	- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

83	**Country context in Angular**
84	
85	- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
86	  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
87	  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
88	  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
89	  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
90	- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
91	  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
92	- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
93	  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
94	  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
95	- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
96	  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
97	- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
98	  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
99	  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
100	  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
101	- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
102	  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
103	  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
104	  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.
105	
106	**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**
107	
108	| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
109	|---|---|---|---|
110	| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
111	| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
112	| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
113	| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
114	| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
115	| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
116	| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
117	| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |
118	
119	- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
120	  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
121	- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
122	  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
123	  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
124	  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
125	  separate child routes.
126	- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
127	  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
128	  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
129	  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
130	  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
131	  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
132	  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
133	- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
134	  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
135	- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
136	  in their stories, spec §8).
137	- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
138	  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).
139	
140	### Consequences
141	
142	- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
143	  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
144	- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
145	- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
146	  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
147	  code-backed rules.
148	- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
149	  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
150	- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
151	  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
152	  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
153	- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
154	  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
155	  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
156	- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
157	  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
158	- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
159	  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
160	- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
161	  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
162	- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
163	  HC1, US-01-Q-27).
164	
165	### Strongest argument against
166	
167	Option B (i18n locales `es-CO` / `es-CL`) gives per-country `key` uniqueness for free: Strapi
168	scopes its `unique` check by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and the admin lets
169	editors fill one country's content from another's. Option A gives up both: uniqueness per country
170	needs custom server code that we must write, test and keep working across Strapi upgrades, and
171	editors have no tool to copy the CO form to CL. Making the country list content also means the
172	country chooser and the unknown-country page depend on Strapi being reachable, where a hard-coded
173	list would not.
174	
175	**Why we accept it:** option B copies non-localised attributes to every locale on save (verified
176	in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong checkbox on a price silently overwrites the other
177	country's value; it mixes language with market and still needs a second mechanism for country
178	metadata (D3, D4). The uniqueness middleware is one small, tested piece, the front end also drops
179	duplicates (AC-14), copying is a minor cost with two countries, and the Strapi dependency is
180	surfaced as a load error with "Reintentar", never as a wrong "not available".
181	
182	### Confirmation
183	
184	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
185	  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
186	  (AC-22).
187	- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
188	  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
189	  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).

191	  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
192	  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
193	- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).
194

## 1. Summary

A visual redesign of the whole quoting wizard (country chooser, step 1 form, plan list, summary,
payment and confirmation) on a tokenized design system, for people in Colombia and Chile on
phone, tablet and desktop. It adds country flags and a per-country accent, icons, an accessible
custom select and date picker (replacing the browser's native ones), a step indicator, step
transitions, skeletons and micro-animations that all honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, a
mobile-first responsive layout with 44 × 44 px targets, and self-hosted typography. Behaviour,
validation, stored values, routes and the Strapi contracts do not change; the existing tests keep
passing with the same strength, adapted only where a native element is replaced (§11.1).

## 2. Scope

**In scope**

- A token file (primitive → semantic → component) and the restyling of every existing page and
  shared component through tokens only.
- Theme, palette, gradients, dotted background texture, type scale, two font families
  self-hosted (US-04-Q-01, Q-03, Q-08).
- Flags of CO and CL as SVG on the country chooser and in a new wizard header; per-country accent
  token (US-04-Q-02, Q-10).
- One icon library; icons inside step 1 inputs (by field key, with a default), in the step
  indicator, plan cards (check-circle in coverage and benefit lists), help, error and success
  messages (US-04-Q-09).
- Custom select (with search for long lists) and custom date picker (typed entry, calendar with
  month and year navigation, `minAge`-disabled days), built on accessible primitives, bound to the
  existing Signal Forms model (ADR-0004), with bottom sheet on mobile (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11,
  Q-12, Q-13).
- New interface microcopy owned by the front end (§8.1).
- Step indicator, step enter transition, hover/focus/active/disabled states, soft validation
  feedback, skeletons, interactive plan cards, summary and confirmation micro-animations
  (US-04-Q-14..Q-17).
- `prefers-reduced-motion`, responsive layout at 360 × 740, 768 × 1024 and 1280 × 800.
- Adapting existing tests where a native element is replaced, as listed in §11.1, and new tests.
- After screenshots in `docs/qa/US-04/after/` (US-04-Q-19).

**Out of scope**

- Any change to routes, guards, the wizard state, validation rules or messages, prices, masking,
  payment simulation, or the Strapi schema, seed, permissions and proxy (story: "Logic, the
  contracts with Strapi and the texts that come from Strapi do not change").
- Rewriting help texts, placeholders or error messages that come from Strapi (US-04-Q-07).
- A light theme or a theme switch, unless US-04-Q-01 says otherwise.
- An in-wizard country switcher (US-01-Q-02 stands).
- Changing the native `number`, `text`, `checkbox` and `radio` controls into custom widgets; they
  are restyled only.
- Logos, names, slogans or texts of any real insurer or company; a brand name for the product.
- Adoption of the third-party design skills `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable`, `frontend-design`: they
  are evaluated separately (task US-04-T-01); this spec does not rely on them.

## 3. Glossary

Terms of the US-01..US-03 glossaries keep their meaning.

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Token | A CSS custom property declared in the single token file (BR-01). |
| Primitive / semantic / component token | Raw values (`--primitive-violet-500`), roles (`--color-text-muted`, `--space-4`), and per-component bindings (`--button-primary-bg`). Components use semantic or component tokens only. |
| Loose value | A literal colour, length, font, shadow, gradient, duration, easing or z-index in a component style instead of a `var(--…)` (allowed literals in BR-01). |
| Country accent | The per-country accent colour token, set from the current country context (BR-03). |
| Custom select | The design-system replacement for a `select` field: a WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox popup (BR-05). |
| Searchable select | A custom select whose option count reaches the search threshold; typing filters the options (US-04-Q-11). |
| Date field | The design-system replacement for a `date` field: a text box for typed entry plus an "Elegir fecha" button that opens the calendar (BR-06). |
| Calendar | The WAI-ARIA date picker dialog opened from the date field. |
| Shown value | What a control displays: the option label of a custom select (the prompt "Selecciona una opción" when empty), the dd/mm/aaaa text of a date field. |
| Stored value | The value in the editing model and in the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003, ADR-0004): option `value`, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `''`. Unchanged by US-04. |
| Panel | The popup of a custom select or the calendar: an anchored popover on wide screens, a bottom sheet on narrow screens (US-04-Q-13). |
| Wizard header | New top bar on the wizard pages with the product name and the country chip (flag + country name). |
| Step indicator | New progress display of the three wizard steps (US-04-Q-17). |

## 5. Acceptance criteria

The story has no Gherkin scenarios, so every AC is derived. Conventions:

- "I completed step 1 in Colombia / Chile" uses the values of US-01-AC-04 / US-02 §5 conventions;
  the date is typed as "15/05/1990" (stored "1990-05-15").
- Today is pinned to **2026-11-21** unless a scenario says otherwise.
- "Narrow" is 360 × 740, "tablet" 768 × 1024, "desktop" 1280 × 800 CSS px.
- Copy in quotes that is not Strapi content is in §8.1.

### US-04-AC-01 — Tokens in one file, no loose values (derived from US-04-BR-01)

```gherkin
Scenario: Tokens in one file, no loose values
  Given the production style files of frontend/src
  Then exactly one file declares custom properties, in three tiers with distinct prefixes
  And no other style file contains a hex, rgb(), hsl(), oklch() or named colour, a px/rem/em length outside @media and @container conditions,
    a font-family name, a box-shadow or gradient literal, a ms/s duration, a cubic-bezier() or a numeric z-index
  And no component style file references a primitive token
  And every breakpoint used in a @media or @container condition is one of the breakpoints documented in the token file
```

### US-04-AC-02 — AA contrast of the token pairs (derived from US-04-BR-02)

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: AA contrast of the token pairs
  Given the token file declares the pair <foreground> on <background> as used in the UI
  When the WCAG 2.2 contrast ratio is computed (at every stop of a gradient background, and against the dotted texture composited at its opacity)
  Then the ratio is at least <minimum>

  Examples:
    | foreground                         | background                               | minimum |
    | body text                          | page background                          | 4.5     |
    | muted text (help, captions)        | page background and card surface         | 4.5     |
    | error text                         | page background and card surface         | 4.5     |
    | primary button text                | primary button background (every stop)   | 4.5     |
    | text on the recommended card       | recommended card gradient (every stop)   | 4.5     |
    | display heading gradient text      | page background (every stop)             | 3       |
    | focus indicator                    | page background and card surface         | 3       |
    | input and card border              | page background and card surface         | 3       |
    | country accent (each country)      | page background and header surface       | 3       |
```

The list of pairs is declared next to the tokens (format set by the ADR) so the test reads it
rather than guessing. Display headings meet 3:1 only if they are large text (BR-02).

## 6. Gaps and open questions

Gaps marked **[Blocks HC1]** change an approved rule of US-01..US-03, an accepted ADR, or the
scope, so they need an explicit answer. For the others the proposed default applies if the human
does not answer. **[ADR]** marks gaps the architect resolves in an ADR (§10) in parallel to HC1.

| ID | Gap | Why it matters | Proposed default | Human answer |

Tokens are structured (semantic tier) so a light theme can be added later by redefining semantic tokens only. Alternative: both, following `prefers-color-scheme`, no switch (+ AC-02 rows per theme, double screenshots). | |
| US-04-Q-02 | **[Blocks HC1] [ADR]** Per-country flag and accent vs ADR-0001 ("No country code, name or list exists in front-end code"; review grep for `'(CO\|CL)'`). One of the two must give. | A presentation-only **country-visuals map** in one front-end file, keyed by ISO code (`CO`, `CL` → flag SVG and accent token values), with a neutral fallback (globe icon, brand accent) for any other published country, so adding a country stays content-only (AC-03). The architect amends ADR-0001 (new ADR or a section of the design-system ADR marked as amending ADR-0001) and narrows its review grep to allow only that file. ## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA; WAI-ARIA APG combobox (select-only and list autocomplete) and
  date picker dialog patterns; visible focus on the focused element; Tab order unchanged except the
  "Elegir fecha" stop; one `h1` per page; decorative icons and flags hidden; `forced-colors`
  fallbacks for gradient text and borders; screen reader pass at HC3 (NVDA or VoiceOver) on the
  select, the calendar and the step indicator.
- **Responsive:** mobile-first CSS; 320–1440 CSS px with no horizontal scroll (verified at 360,
  768, 1280); 44 × 44 px targets; bottom sheet below 600 px.
- **Multi-country:** one build; no country branch except the presentation map of US-04-Q-02;
  calendar names and date formatting from `Intl` and the country `localeTag`; the date text format
  is the same for every country.
- **Security / privacy:** no third-party origin at runtime (fonts, icons, flags self-hosted, so no
  new CSP or proxy change); no value of the form in logs; no `innerHTML` for icons or flags (the
  existing static guard applies: icons and flags are components or inline template SVG).
- **Performance:** icons imported individually; fonts subset WOFF2, at most the weights used;
  the production build stays within the existing `angular.json` budgets (initial 500 kB warning,
  1 MB error; component styles 4 kB warning, 8 kB error), or the ADR justifies a change; no
  animation runs on layout properties (transform and opacity only).
- **Maintainability:** tokens in one file; new shared components under `src/app/shared/`
  (CLAUDE.md §6 naming, for example `custom-select.ts` → `CustomSelect`, `date-field.ts` →
  `DateField`, `step-indicator.ts` → `StepIndicator`; final names by the ADR or the developer).
- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, docs English.

     arriving heading (unchanged).

## 1. Summary

A visual redesign of the whole quoting wizard (country chooser, step 1 form, plan list, summary,
payment and confirmation) on a tokenized design system, for people in Colombia and Chile on
phone, tablet and desktop. It adds country flags and a per-country accent, icons, an accessible
custom select and date picker (replacing the browser's native ones), a step indicator, step
transitions, skeletons and micro-animations that all honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, a
mobile-first responsive layout with 44 × 44 px targets, and self-hosted typography. Behaviour,
validation, stored values, routes and the Strapi contracts do not change; the existing tests keep
passing with the same strength, adapted only where a native element is replaced (§11.1).

## 2. Scope

**In scope**

- A token file (primitive → semantic → component) and the restyling of every existing page and
  shared component through tokens only.
- Theme, palette, gradients, dotted background texture, type scale, two font families
  self-hosted (US-04-Q-01, Q-03, Q-08).
- Flags of CO and CL as SVG on the country chooser and in a new wizard header; per-country accent
  token (US-04-Q-02, Q-10).
- One icon library; icons inside step 1 inputs (by field key, with a default), in the step
  indicator, plan cards (check-circle in coverage and benefit lists), help, error and success
  messages (US-04-Q-09).
- Custom select (with search for long lists) and custom date picker (typed entry, calendar with
  month and year navigation, `minAge`-disabled days), built on accessible primitives, bound to the
  existing Signal Forms model (ADR-0004), with bottom sheet on mobile (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11,
  Q-12, Q-13).
- New interface microcopy owned by the front end (§8.1).
- Step indicator, step enter transition, hover/focus/active/disabled states, soft validation
  feedback, skeletons, interactive plan cards, summary and confirmation micro-animations
  (US-04-Q-14..Q-17).
- `prefers-reduced-motion`, responsive layout at 360 × 740, 768 × 1024 and 1280 × 800.
- Adapting existing tests where a native element is replaced, as listed in §11.1, and new tests.
- After screenshots in `docs/qa/US-04/after/` (US-04-Q-19).

**Out of scope**

- Any change to routes, guards, the wizard state, validation rules or messages, prices, masking,
  payment simulation, or the Strapi schema, seed, permissions and proxy (story: "Logic, the
  contracts with Strapi and the texts that come from Strapi do not change").
- Rewriting help texts, placeholders or error messages that come from Strapi (US-04-Q-07).
- A light theme or a theme switch, unless US-04-Q-01 says otherwise.
- An in-wizard country switcher (US-01-Q-02 stands).
- Changing the native `number`, `text`, `checkbox` and `radio` controls into custom widgets; they
  are restyled only.
- Logos, names, slogans or texts of any real insurer or company; a brand name for the product.
- Adoption of the third-party design skills `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable`, `frontend-design`: they
  are evaluated separately (task US-04-T-01); this spec does not rely on them.

## 3. Glossary

Terms of the US-01..US-03 glossaries keep their meaning.

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Token | A CSS custom property declared in the single token file (BR-01). |
| Primitive / semantic / component token | Raw values (`--primitive-violet-500`), roles (`--color-text-muted`, `--space-4`), and per-component bindings (`--button-primary-bg`). Components use semantic or component tokens only. |
| Loose value | A literal colour, length, font, shadow, gradient, duration, easing or z-index in a component style instead of a `var(--…)` (allowed literals in BR-01). |
| Country accent | The per-country accent colour token, set from the current country context (BR-03). |
| Custom select | The design-system replacement for a `select` field: a WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox popup (BR-05). |
| Searchable select | A custom select whose option count reaches the search threshold; typing filters the options (US-04-Q-11). |
| Date field | The design-system replacement for a `date` field: a text box for typed entry plus an "Elegir fecha" button that opens the calendar (BR-06). |
| Calendar | The WAI-ARIA date picker dialog opened from the date field. |
| Shown value | What a control displays: the option label of a custom select (the prompt "Selecciona una opción" when empty), the dd/mm/aaaa text of a date field. |
| Stored value | The value in the editing model and in the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003, ADR-0004): option `value`, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `''`. Unchanged by US-04. |
| Panel | The popup of a custom select or the calendar: an anchored popover on wide screens, a bottom sheet on narrow screens (US-04-Q-13). |
| Wizard header | New top bar on the wizard pages with the product name and the country chip (flag + country name). |
| Step indicator | New progress display of the three wizard steps (US-04-Q-17). |
